## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.

70	- Promotions engine and multi-currency/FX pricebook setup
71	- CI workflow split — two complementary workflows, each with a clear role:
72	  - `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): `unit-tests` (Vitest) + `storybook-test` (Storybook `play` + `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `storybook test --ci`) run in parallel; `e2e-browserstack` on release PRs only. **`storybook-test` job is wired but pending `@storybook/addon-test` and `@storybook/addon-a11y` installation (feature/storybook-v10 upgrade task).**
73	  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
74	- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
75	- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
76	- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
77	  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
78	  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
79	  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
80	  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
81	    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
82	    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
83	    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
84	    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
85	    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
86	  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**

Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Separately, the source note now records the platform CDN as Akamai (SFCC default), which sits against existing Cloudflare carry-forward references — confirm the CDN platform of record (no asset-migration impact either way).
- **PRC-43 Global-e cartridge customer-group catalogue prices:** Open with Global-e — does the cartridge honour customer-group catalogue prices (VIC) at international checkout? Also: how do VIC customers currently receive discounts at Global-e checkout in M2? Do not assume VIC pricing flows through Global-e until confirmed.
- **CFD-070 guest account creation flow:** Dependent on the guest journey design — open.
- **CFD-045 BOPIS seeding mechanism:** Open — how Collect in Boutique availability is seeded into checkout still TBC.
- **PAY-022 Adyen CVC config:** Confirm CVC-on-saved-card configuration with Adyen. PWA behaviour (re-entry required) is Confirmed.
- **PAY-047/048/049 fraud hold scope:** Adyen/NewStore-owned per IC; PWA-side display behaviour not yet signed off.
- **OM-002 MuleSoft order export gating:** Sign-off pending on the exact attribute set passed at order export.
- **OM-017/018 NewStore order status taxonomy:** SFCC displays raw MuleSoft status; mapping list still open.
- **OM-034 back-in-stock FIFO email logic:** Sign-off pending.
- **DLV-012 free-shipping thresholds:** Per-delivery-method per-storefront rate card updated; re-sign-off pending.
- **CAI-041 location-aware boutique inventory fallback:** Flagged as potential enhancement (RJ 25.05) — not in launch scope until confirmed.
- **RRC-030 tax/duties display location:** Confirm whether tax/duties appear in My Account vs Narvar/Global-e portals only.
- **CRM-022 international Retail Rewards via Global-e:** Not scoped; needs Global-e discussion.
- **CRM-048 / CRM-100 saved-address cap:** RJ proposes 20; IC "we can do this" — working target 20, formal sign-off pending.

Note: Move-to-Wishlist (CAI-004/008) is **confirmed authenticated-only** at launch — guests are prompted to log in; guest wishlist is a logged enhancement out of scope for go-live.
- **Returns-link eligibility logic (ENH-014):** To be sized. Intended logic (not yet confirmed): show the Returns link only if the order contains returnable items (via product attribute); window = 15 days from delivery completion date, else 28 days from order creation date if no delivery completion date. Hard dependency: the delivery completion date must be passed back via MuleSoft.
- **Address validation on free-text addresses (CFD-024):** PO Box / Parcel Locker blocking is Confirmed. NEW VR/RT review request (not scoped): "Current magento behaviour lets a user checkout with a very random address with no error messaging. Can this be reviewed?" — broader address-validity enhancement, unscoped.
- **SSO scope (CRM-001):** Sheet only says "to be considered for go-live (ENH tab — to be discussed)". Treat as Open. Note: Social login (Apple/Google) is separately confirmed via ENH-004 (see entry above) and is the only SSO surface in scope for launch.
- **PRC-46 coupon handling at Global-e:** Workbook shows Confirmed 2026-06-24, but sign-off is conditional — "only if Global-e can support." Confirm with Global-e that the SFCC cartridge can apply and validate coupon codes at international checkout before implementing.
- **PRC-53 Global-e digital gift card currencies:** Currency coverage for digital gift cards at Global-e checkout to be confirmed.

24	// font-family values like "'Futura Round', sans-serif", outputting just "sans-serif".

61	  },
62	};

content.thinking:
I'm spotting a real mismatch: globalStyles' `.zimm-text-h1` maps the heading font family to FONT_MEDIUM, while the textStyles `heading1` definition uses FONT_REGULAR instead, so the two systems disagree on heading weight.

Checking further, I notice FONT_MEDIUM and FONT_REGULAR actually resolve to the identical string value, which masks the drift in practice but is itself a smell worth flagging as low-priority duplication. I'm also noting that `.zimm-text-link-lg` in globalStyles hardcodes a letter-spacing value outside the token registry, and that it additionally defines color, transition, and hover/focus states that the textStyles equivalent lacks entirely — meaning the two surfaces aren't truly 1:1 for interactive styling, which may be intentional but is worth calling out.

I'm now counting the text classes in both globalStyles and textStyles to confirm they line up one-to-one — both come out to 22, and combined with grid, button, form, and focus classes the total reaches 36, matching what the commit message claims. Next I want to dig into the app-config file, the test file, and the remaining foundation files, and then check for tier violations.

This surfaces a major governance concern: the foundation theme directory is explicitly protected by Hard Rule #3 (no direct edits, must go through the UI designer) and sits at Tier 1, same as the theme index file and the frozen/protected files rules which require both squad leads plus the integration lead to sign off. The derived AI config files also need verification that they were regenerated through the proper sync script rather than edited directly, since there's a pre-commit hook blocking that. Meanwhile the component-level theme files and the app-config component fall under Tier 2, so this change spans two protection tiers at once — which trips Hard Rule #10 requiring a pause to confirm scope before touching multiple tiers in one change. I want to verify the AI rules sync check passes, then read the app-config file and run the sync check, lint, and tests.

content.thinking:
I've confirmed empirically that in a Storybook-equivalent mount without the app's global config, 44 distinct `--zimm-*` CSS variables are referenced but none are actually defined—every single one is unresolved. This is a reproducible issue affecting the preview setup and the theme test file.

Now I'm cleaning up the probe directory and moving on to check a few more things: the CSS/bundle size impact from all the emitted classes and variables, font loading behavior given that only 2 of 10 declared font weights are actually used (so the rest are dead weight but not downloaded), and accessibility concerns around the focus ring styling against WCAG 2.2's newer focus-appearance criteria.

I'm finding a real issue: the focus ring color matches one of the dark background colors exactly, meaning on dark surfaces the focus indicator would be completely invisible — a WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible and 1.4.11 non-text contrast failure, since there's an inverse form row variant for dark backgrounds but no corresponding inverse focus ring treatment. I'm verifying this by checking how the focus-visible styles reference the border-focus variable, and noticing the same pattern repeats in the large text link's focus style.

I'm also checking color contrast on the primary button's hover state, where white text sits on a gray background (#969696). Calculating the relative luminance and contrast ratio gives roughly 2.96:1, which fails the WCAG AA requirement of 4.5:1 for normal text — a genuine accessibility defect on an interactive hover state.

I'm also noting that disabled button states are exempt from contrast requirements under WCAG 1.4.3, so the disabled text/background pairing isn't an issue. But the muted text color (#969696) on white also computes to 2.96:1, failing 4.5:1 if it's used for actual body text rather than decorative elements — I want to check where that token gets applied before flagging it, and also verify the inverse-grey variant used on dark backgrounds.

Continuing the contrast ratio checks, the error color passes at 8.70:1, and the success and store-closed status colors look like they'll pass too based on their luminance calculations.

I'm also noticing several other hardcoded values bypassing the token registry—button min-width, form row min-height, icon padding, outline offset—which is worth flagging as a consistency issue per the design system guidelines. # `feature/design-tokens-implementation-to-dev` — In-Depth Analysis

**Position:** 3 commits ahead of `develop`, 0 behind. Pushed to origin, no PR open. 35 files, +1755/−91.

---

## 1. What the branch actually does

It lands the Figma-To-React handover as **two parallel token surfaces** on top of one source:

| Surface | Where | Consumed by |
|---|---|---|
| Chakra scales (`colors`, `fonts`, `textStyles`, `space`, `borderWidths`, `breakpoints`) | `foundation/*.ts` → `theme/index.ts` | Chakra props, `textStyle="body1"` |
| CSS custom properties (122 `--zimm-*`) | [zimmTokens.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts) → `<Global>` in `_app-config` | 36 `.zimm-*` global classes in [globalStyles.ts](overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts) |

Plus: 10 self-hosted Futura Round `.woff2` files (336 KB total) with `@font-face` + preload of the 2 weights actually used, 3 Foundation Storybook stories, and 143 tests.

The deliberate non-registration of `fontSizes`, `transition`, and `sizes` ([index.ts:29-49](overrides/app/theme/index.ts:29)) is the strongest decision in the branch — four Zimmermann font-size keys collide with Chakra defaults used at ~199 base call sites, and the tests actively guard against a future remap.

## 2. Health checks — all green

- `npx tsc --noEmit` → **exit 0**
- `npx vitest run` → **143 passed / 143** (3 files)
- `npm run lint` → 19 errors, but **all in files this branch never touches** (`contentful/experiences/definitions.ts`, `header/index.tsx`, `routes.tsx`) — pre-existing on `develop`. Note there is *no lint job in `qa.yml`*, so this is ungated drift either way.
- `npm run sync:ai-rules:check` → all `.cursor/` + `.github/copilot-instructions.md` derivations in sync.

---

## 3. The one finding I'd block the PR on

**The `--zimm-*` registry is injected by a component, not by the theme — so the theme is only correct inside the app.**

`_app-config/index.tsx:277` is the *only* place `--zimm-*` variables are ever defined (I grepped the whole repo). But the Tier 2 component overrides now reference them directly:

```
button.ts    border: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid'
listMenu.ts  height: 'var(--zimm-border-width-default)'   ← the ::after hover underline
listMenu.ts  right:  'var(--zimm-scale-700)'
header.ts    fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-3xs)'
```

`.storybook/preview.tsx` mounts `<ChakraProvider theme={theme}>` and **never renders `_app-config`**. I reproduced that exact mount and measured the emitted CSS:

```
referencedCount: 44
definedCount:     0
unresolvedCount: 44
```

Every one unresolved. In Storybook that means primary/secondary buttons render **with no border**, the ListMenu hover underline has **zero height**, and all 36 `.zimm-*` classes lose their type and colour — which defeats the purpose of the three Foundation stories that were added in the same commit.

The same boundary applies to any future harness that mounts the theme without `AppConfig`. The existing `rendered output` tests in `index.test.tsx:310-335` pass only because they assert literal values (`borderRadius: 0px`, `textTransform: uppercase`), not var-backed ones — so the suite would not catch this.

The stated reason for the `<Global>` workaround ([index.ts:21-24](overrides/app/theme/index.ts:21)) — Chakra strips quotes from font-family values — is real, but it applies to **3 font-family vars**, not the other 119. The fix is small; the awkward part is that `.storybook/` is Tier 1 frozen, so the cleanest fix (a preview decorator) needs Integration sign-off. Emitting the `:root` block from `styles.global` for everything except the font families keeps it inside Tier 1/Tier 2 files you already own.

*Secondary effect of the same root cause:* the code's own comment at `_app-config/index.tsx:114-118` notes Emotion places these `<style>` tags in `<body>`, not `<head>`, under SSR. That's fine for the fonts (the preload solves discovery) but it means the token `:root` block is also body-injected — worth a look against the ≤2s p75 LCP budget once you can measure it.

---

## 4. Accessibility — WCAG 2.2 AA failures in the token values

You target AA. I computed contrast across the new palette:

| Pair | Ratio | AA text (4.5) |
|---|---|---|
| Primary button label on **hover** — `#ffffff` on `#969696` | **2.96** | ✗ |
| `text.muted` `#969696` on white | **2.96** | ✗ |
| `text.muted` `#969696` on `bg-01` | **2.79** | ✗ |
| `status.storeClosed` `#d67600` on white | **3.26** | ✗ (passes 3:1 non-text) |
| Focus ring `#191919` on `bg-05` `#191919` | **1.00** | ✗ |
| Focus ring `#191919` on `bg-06` `#282828` | **1.19** | ✗ |

Two of these are structural, not cosmetic:

- **Primary button hover drops to 2.96:1.** A user hovering the main CTA loses the label. This is `--zimm-color-action-primary-bg-hover` straight from the handover.
- **There is no inverse focus ring.** `--zimm-focus-ring` is hard-coded `1px solid #191919`, and `globalStyles.ts` already ships `.zimm-form-row-inverse` and `.zimm-form-control-inverse` for dark surfaces — so dark contexts are explicitly anticipated, but focus becomes invisible on them (SC 2.4.7 + 1.4.11).

All of these live in Tier 1 `foundation/`, which Hard Rule #3 puts with the UI designer. These are designer decisions to raise, not values to change here.

## 5. Governance

`gh api user` → `marcelannavarro`, confirmed a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`. The verified-session exception in AGENTS.md applies, and none of the four absolute-never files (`ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`) are touched.

Two things still need naming in the PR body:

1. **The change spans Tier 1 and Tier 2** (Hard Rule #10) — `foundation/` + `theme/index.ts` + `static/fonts/` at Tier 1; `theme/components/`, `globalStyles.ts`, `_app-config/` at Tier 2.
2. **`.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` and `protectedFiles.md` were edited.** The edits are good — they correctly extend Tier 1 to the three new foundation files and `static/fonts/`, and place `globalStyles.ts` at Tier 2 with a clear rationale. But Governance files carry the "both squad leads + Integration lead" owner, a stronger bar than the ordinary verified-session exception. CODEOWNERS will force that review anyway; just don't let it surprise anyone.

## 6. Open items the branch itself flags — these need the designer before merge

The commits are unusually honest about what's unresolved, which is good, but it's a list someone has to close:

- `text.inverseGrey` — handover contradicts itself, `#969696` vs `#939393` ([colour.ts:50-52](overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts:50))
- All motion tokens marked **PROVISIONAL, pending sign-off** ([motion.ts:2-4](overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts:2))
- Button heights: prototype 50/41px vs handover 52/40px — prototype kept ([button.ts:83-86](overrides/app/theme/components/button.ts:83))
- Nav letter-spacing: prototype `0.02em` vs design system `0px` — prototype kept, in two files
- `border.error` has no handover counterpart
- `FONT_SERIF` (Source Serif 4) resolves to Georgia — no `.woff2` ships
- `FONT_REGULAR` and `FONT_MEDIUM` are **byte-identical strings**, so every "these two surfaces agree" test comparing them passes trivially

## 7. Doc drift

- `.docs/architecture.md:136` still lists foundation as "colour, fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing" — missing `motion.ts`, `sizes.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`, and the `globalStyles.ts`/`static/fonts/` tier assignments. `frozenFiles.md` was updated; `architecture.md` wasn't.
- `.docs/memory/projectState.md:46` claims tokens are already "finalised" — written before this work and now actively misleading given §6.
- **No CSS budget exists in CI.** `bundlesize` covers only `main.js` and `vendor.js`; `projectState.md`'s claimed `main.css < 50 kB` SIT gate was never implemented. This branch's CSS growth is ungated. (Saved to memory.)

## 8. Smaller notes

- The 36 `.zimm-*` classes have **exactly one consumer** — `.zimm-grid` in `spacing.stories.tsx:79`. `textStyle` is used only in the new stories and tests. Nothing in production consumes either surface yet, including the existing Header override. That's reasonable for a foundation PR, but it means none of this is exercised by a real page.
- Hardcoded values that bypass the registry inside `globalStyles.ts`: `minWidth: '80px'`, `minHeight: '36px'`, `padding: '8px'`, `outlineOffset: '2px'`, `letterSpacing: '-0.14px'`, and three `transition: ... 0.15s` literals — against the no-hardcoded-values rule in `css.md`.
- Stories follow conventions correctly (`Foundation/` titles, `Default` exports).
- **Uncommitted in your working tree:** 5 translation files (`header.button.assistive_msg.search`) — build artifacts unrelated to this branch, in a Tier 2 Integration-owned path. Keep them out of this PR.

---

## Recommendation

The work is high quality and the reasoning in the comments is better than most. Sequencing I'd suggest:

1. **Fix the var-resolution boundary** — move the `:root` block into `styles.global`, keeping the three font-family vars on the `<Global>` escape hatch. Add a test asserting zero unresolved `--zimm-*` in a bare `ChakraProvider` mount, so this can't silently regress.
2. **Take §4 and §6 to the UI designer as one list.** The hover-state and focus-ring contrast failures are the two that shouldn't ship.
3. **Update `architecture.md` and `projectState.md`** in the same PR — the rule files were updated, these weren't.
4. Then `cr review --light --base develop` per the workflow, and open the PR flagging the Tier 1 + Tier 2 span and the governance-file edits.

I haven't changed anything — this was read-only. Want me to start on (1)?

## 1. Up to date with develop? Yes — completely.

```
merge-base:      d9c3c40
origin/develop:  d9c3c40   ← identical
```

Your local `develop` is also in sync with origin (0/0). The branch is **0 behind, 3 ahead**, and `git merge-tree` finds no conflicts. Develop's last movement was PR #51 (US-intl storefront) on 8 Aug; this branch's work started after it. Nothing to rebase or merge in.

---

## 2. The diff, sorted against "is this a master design file?"

1,755 added / 91 removed across 35 files. Here's how that splits:

| Category | Lines | Verdict vs. your intent |
|---|---|---|
| **A. Master design files** | 854 + 336 KB fonts | ✅ This is the point |
| **B. Wiring to make A reachable** | 177 | ✅ Necessary |
| **C. Proof & visual reference** | 621 | ✅ Appropriate |
| **D. Governance bookkeeping** | 60 | ⚠️ Defensible, escalates review |
| **E. Auto-generated byproduct** | 4 | ⚠️ Noise |
| **F. Component retrofits** | 39 | ⚠️ **Doesn't fit "foundational"** |

### A — The master design system (854 lines)

This is genuinely foundational, and it's complete in the dimensions it covers:

- **[colour.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts)** (+83/−16) — the full palette in two layers: brand primitives (`grey.900`, `ivory.400`, `coral/green/orange/red.500`, opacity ramp) and semantic aliases on top (`text.*`, `background.01–07`, `border.*`, `status.*`, `link.*`, `icon.*`, `action.primary.*`, `action.secondary.*`). The two-layer split is the right shape — components consume the semantic names, so a primitive can be re-pointed without touching call sites.
- **[typography.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts)** (+113/−31) — 22 named text styles, each mapped to its Figma name in a comment (`ZIM/h1-strong`, `ZIM/Mobile/Body1`, `ZIM/Product-name`, `ZIM/Price`, `ZIM/Footer`). Registered as Chakra `textStyles`, so the usage is `<Text textStyle="body1">` rather than loose font-size props.
- **[zimmTokens.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts)** (+184) — the same design system expressed a second time as 122 `--zimm-*` CSS custom properties with fully-resolved literal values.
- **[globalStyles.ts](overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts)** (+413) — 36 `.zimm-*` global classes built on those variables: 22 typography, 7 button, 5 form-field, 1 grid, 1 focus utility.
- **[fonts.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts)** + **10 × FuturaRound `.woff2`** (336 KB) — the licensed brand face, self-hosted, 5 weights × roman/oblique. This is the single most "master" asset in the PR: it's the brand's actual typeface, not a config.
- **[spacing.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts)**, **[sizes.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts)**, **[motion.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts)** (+53 combined) — spacing scale + border widths, icon/action dimensions, and duration/easing.

**On the double surface (Chakra + CSS vars):** this is the one structural decision worth understanding, because it's what most of the complexity is paying for. The design system is written down twice so that a component can be styled *either* by a Chakra prop *or* by a handover CSS class and land on the same pixel. `index.test.tsx` exists mostly to enforce that they can't drift. It's defensible — it lets you paste handover markup and have it look right — but it doubles the surface area of every future token change. Worth a conscious yes/no from you before it becomes 8 more sprints of habit.

### B — Wiring (177 lines)

- **[_app-config/index.tsx](overrides/app/components/_app-config/index.tsx)** (+127) — the largest non-foundation file, but ~110 of those lines are the 10 `@font-face` declarations plus a `<link rel=preload>` for the 2 weights actually in the type scale. That's font payload delivery, not app logic. The remaining ~17 lines inject the `:root` variable block.
- **theme/index.ts** (+36/−1), **foundation/index.ts** (+5/−2) — composition and barrel exports. The bulk of `index.ts`'s addition is the comment block explaining which Chakra scales are deliberately *not* remapped.
- **types/vendor.d.ts** (+9) — a `react-helmet` type shim so the preload typechecks.

### C — Proof and visual reference (621 lines)

- **index.test.tsx** (+336) — 127 of the 143 tests. Not busywork: it pins the Chakra↔CSS-var agreement, and guards the four `fontSizes` collisions against a future remap that would silently restyle ~199 base call sites.
- **3 Foundation stories** (+285) — `Foundation/Colour`, `Foundation/Typography`, `Foundation/Spacing`. Correct titles, `Default` exports, token path rendered as text next to every swatch so nothing relies on colour alone.

### D, E — Bookkeeping and noise

- **rules files + `.cursor/` + copilot** (+60/−3) — assigns Tier 1 ownership to the three new foundation files and `static/fonts/`, and puts `globalStyles.ts` at Tier 2. Content is right; it's what pulls squad-lead + Integration-lead review onto the PR.
- **`.claude/registry/components.md`** (+4/−4) — auto-staged by the pre-commit hook. Two of the four changed lines (`Field` consumers 11→12, `Register` 3→6) have **nothing to do with this branch** — the branch adds no consumer of either. They're catch-up from develop moving since the registry was last regenerated on 31 Jul. Harmless, but it's unrelated churn sitting in a "design tokens" diff.

---

## 3. The one part that doesn't fit your stated intent

**F — the three component retrofits** ([button.ts](overrides/app/theme/components/button.ts), [header.ts](overrides/app/theme/components/header.ts), [listMenu.ts](overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts), +39/−29).

Most of what's in them is fine and mechanical — swapping `'#454545'` → `action.primary.bgPressed`, `'white'` → `background.07`, `'1px'` → the border-width token. That's exactly "apply the foundation."

But two changes are **component-level design decisions that contradict the master files landing in the same PR**:

- `button.ts` sizes stay at the prototype's **50px / 41px**; the handover's action tokens — shipped in `sizes.ts` in this very diff — say **52px / 40px**.
- `header.ts` and `listMenu.ts` keep the prototype's **`letterSpacing: '0.02em'`**; `.zimm-text-nav` and `textStyles.navigation` — both shipped in this diff — say **`0px`**.

The code is honest about it (there's a comment at each site saying it's unresolved with the UI designer). But the effect is that the first three consumers of the master design system are already documented exceptions to it. For a PR whose job is to establish the foundation, that's the wrong precedent to set on day one — it makes "the prototype wins over the design system" the default reading for whoever builds the next component.

I'd either resolve those two with the designer before merge, or split the three component files out into a follow-up so the foundation PR is purely the foundation.

## 4. Gaps worth knowing about

Not scope creep — the opposite, things a "master design files" PR might be expected to carry:

- **No shadows foundation.** `Foundation/Shadows` is a listed Storybook category and nothing defines it. Possibly correct for this brand (the header override explicitly sets `boxShadow: 'none'`), but it should be a stated decision rather than an omission.
- **`FONT_SERIF` has no font file.** Source Serif 4 is declared as the decorative accent and `textStyles.serif` / `.zimm-text-serif` both reference it, but no `.woff2` ships — it silently renders Georgia today.
- **`gridSystem.ts` was not touched.** `globalStyles.ts` imports `breakpoints` and `grid` from it, so the grid foundation pre-existed and is being consumed rather than replaced. No gap, just worth knowing it's the one foundation file not refreshed in this pass.
- **Icons** already have a story (`icons.stories.tsx`, pre-existing) — that category is covered.

---

**Net:** the diff is well-matched to your intent. ~85% of it is master design files, their wiring, and their proof. The parts that aren't are small: 4 lines of registry noise, and 39 lines of component retrofit that carry two decisions which belong with the designer rather than in the foundation PR.

I need to identify which out-of-scope diffs actually help the FED build versus which are just tangential additions, giving a clear keep-or-drop verdict for each rather than hedging on technicalities.

Going through the categories: wiring changes to app-config and theme index files, proof/reference material like tests and stories, governance rule updates across Claude/Cursor/Copilot configs, an auto-generated registry file, and component retrofits starting with the button component.

Recounting the totals, I get 35 files total, with category A (the core design tokens plus woff2 fonts) covering 18 of them, leaving 17 files outside that core scope — matching my breakdown of 4+4+5+1+3.

Now I need to apply a value judgment: does each out-of-scope item actually help a FED developer build components faster or more consistently, starting with the highest-value items that blur the line of what counts as "in scope."

The theme index file is critical — it's what makes the foundation tokens actually reachable, and its comment block documents a dangerous collision between Zimmermann font-size keys and Chakra defaults used across roughly 199 call sites, which could cause silent mis-styling if a developer doesn't know about it. The foundation barrel export is trivial but defines the clean import surface developers will use. And the app-config file is essential since without it the brand typeface won't load.

Without the vendor types file, the font preload won't typecheck and the build blocks entirely, so it's cheap but necessary plumbing. The Foundation stories are the strongest case for genuine value — they're what actually helps a frontend developer build against the design system in practice.

But I need to caveat this hard: these stories currently render wrong due to the var-resolution bug, so their value is contingent on that fix landing first. Moving to `theme/index.test.tsx`, I want to be honest rather than reflexively praising the tests — the collision guards catching unmapped fontSizes/transition/sizes are genuinely valuable as an automated tripwire.

The Chakra↔CSS-var agreement tests are weaker though — most of the 127 tests just confirm two hand-written files derived from the same source still match, which only catches a one-sided edit. My verdict is to keep the file, but its real value is concentrated in maybe 40 of the 336 lines, not the bulk of it.

Moving to the frozenFiles/protectedFiles rules: the static/fonts rationale about a renamed woff2 silently falling back without a build error is a genuinely useful warning, but the rest is mostly ownership routing rather than FED-relevant content. I'd keep it for that one non-obvious failure mode, not for its governance value, and now I'm looking at the .cursor and copilot instruction files next.

These are mechanically derived from the frozenFiles rules via the sync script, so they carry zero independent value — they're just the same content compiled for other tools, enforced by a pre-commit hook and check job, meaning they're not optional but also not a real contribution on their own. The components registry file is similarly zero value, auto-staged by the hook with half its diff being unrelated churn, nothing a FED dev would ever read. Now I'm turning to the three component retrofits, which seem more interesting and worth splitting apart, starting with the token substitution changes.

The token substitutions have real value as worked examples — a FED dev opening the button component sees exactly how it consumes the foundation, making it a template for future components and genuinely useful onboarding material. But the retrofits also use raw CSS variable strings directly in Chakra props, which is exactly the pattern that breaks outside the app and which a dev will now copy, so as a worked example it currently teaches the wrong pattern. The deviations in sizing and letter-spacing also send the message that the prototype overrides the design system, so overall this is highest-value-if-fixed but negative-value-as-is.

Now I want to structure the answer around the two things asked: listing the out-of-scope diffs, and identifying which ones genuinely add value. I'll present the diffs as a table followed by a clear ranked verdict, being decisive about keep, keep-if-fixed, or drop recommendations. I'm tallying up the line counts across the out-of-scope files to see what fraction of the total diff they represent, since that's a useful number to include — it looks like roughly half the added lines fall outside the core token files, which is a striking point worth highlighting.

The user's framing matters here: they explicitly said to set aside technicalities like tier rules or "it's just documentation" and judge purely on whether something helps the FED build. That reframing actually elevates things like the stories and the index.ts comment block, which are "just documentation" but genuinely useful, while demoting governance files that are defensible on tier grounds but low in practical value. That's the sharpest insight to lead with, so I'll make it explicit in the writeup.

17 of 35 files, **901 of 1,755 added lines — 51%** of the diff sits outside the master token files.

| # | File | Lines | Group |
|---|---|---|---|

| 2 | [theme/foundation/index.ts](overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts) | +5/−2 | Wiring |

| 17 | [theme/components/listMenu.ts](overrides/app/theme/components/listMenu.ts) | +13/−10 | Component retrofit |

---

## Which of these actually earn their place

Judged only on: **does this make the next FED developer's component faster, more correct, or more consistent?**

Applying that test rather than the tier/documentation framing flips the usual ranking — the two most valuable items here are both things that would normally get waved through as "just comments" and "just stories," and the least valuable are the ones with the strongest formal justification.

### Tier 1 value — these are the reason to merge, not incidental to it

**#1 `theme/index.ts` — the highest-value non-token file in the entire PR.**

Not because it composes the theme (mechanical), but because of the 20-line comment block at lines 26–49. It documents that four Zimmermann font-size keys (`md`, `xs`, `2xs`, `3xs`) collide with Chakra defaults used at **~199 call sites in the base retail-react-app**, and that `transition` and `sizes` collide too. Zimmermann `md` is 24px; Chakra `md` is 16px.

A FED dev who doesn't know this writes `fontSize="md"`, gets 16px instead of 24px, concludes the theme is broken, and "fixes" it by registering the Zimmermann scale — silently restyling every base component on the site. That comment block is the single thing most likely to prevent a real incident in the first fortnight of FED build. It's a landmine map, not documentation.

**#5–7 The three Foundation stories — the highest-leverage item for the build actually commencing.**

This is what converts 850 lines of TypeScript data into something a developer can *use*. "Which text style for a product name?" is a 5-second visual answer in `Foundation/Typography` versus mentally rendering a 205-line file. `Foundation/Colour` prints the token path as text beside every swatch. `Foundation/Spacing` renders a live `.zimm-grid`.

If you're onboarding developers onto a design system next week, this is the artifact they'll open every day. Nothing else in the out-of-scope list comes close.

**One condition, and it's not optional:** as established, these stories currently render *wrong* — Storybook never mounts `_app-config`, so all 44 `--zimm-*` references resolve to nothing. A reference implementation that displays incorrect values is worse than none, because people will trust it. Their value is entirely contingent on fixing the var-injection boundary first.

**#3 `_app-config/index.tsx` — hard functional dependency.**

The brand typeface is the most visible single element of the design system. Without these 10 `@font-face` declarations the site renders Century Gothic. You cannot meaningfully commence a FED build against a design system whose typeface isn't loading. (This is also where the var-injection fix needs to land.)

**#2, #4 — trivial but non-negotiable.** The barrel export is the import surface; the type shim is what keeps `tsc --noEmit` green. Zero ongoing cost, no argument to have.

### Tier 2 value — real, but concentrated

**#8 `index.test.tsx` (+336).** I'd resist calling all 336 lines valuable.

- The **collision guards** (~40 lines) are genuinely high value — an automated tripwire for exactly the mistake #1's comment warns about. A dev who remaps the font scale gets a red test instead of a silently restyled site.
- The **Chakra↔CSS-var agreement suite** (~100 of the 127 tests) largely asserts that two files written from the same source still match. It would catch a one-sided edit, which is real — but a lot of it is checking that `#191919` equals `#191919`.

Keep it; tests are cheap to carry. Just don't score it as 336 lines of value — it's about 40 lines of insurance and 300 lines of symmetry checking.

**#9–10 the two rules files.** Setting tier politics aside entirely, one paragraph here earns its place on pure engineering merit: the note that renaming or deleting a `.woff2` **silently drops that weight to the fallback stack with no build error and no failing test**. That's a non-obvious failure mode with no other detection anywhere in the repo. The rest is ownership routing.

Keep it for that paragraph, not for the tier assignment.

### Tier 3 — no independent value

**#11–13 the `.cursor/` and copilot files.** Mechanically compiled from #9–10 by `npm run sync:ai-rules`. Zero independent content. Not optional (the pre-commit hook blocks direct edits, and a check job verifies sync), but they contribute nothing on their own — they live or die with #9–10.

**#14 `.claude/registry/components.md`.** Zero value. Auto-staged by the pre-commit hook, and two of its four changed lines (`Field` 11→12, `Register` 3→6) are unrelated catch-up from develop moving since 31 July. No FED developer will ever read it.

### The genuinely contested one

**#15–17 the component retrofits.** Split these — the concept and the execution point in opposite directions.

**The concept is the second-best idea in the PR.** Three worked examples showing how a real component consumes the foundation is exactly what a team starting FED build needs. `'#454545'` → `action.primary.bgPressed`, `'white'` → `background.07` — that's a template someone can copy for the next twenty components.

**The execution currently teaches three things you don't want copied:**

1. Raw `var(--zimm-*)` strings inside Chakra props (`fontSize: 'var(--zimm-font-size-2xs)'`) — the exact pattern that breaks outside the app shell. Every dev who reads `button.ts` as a reference will reproduce it.
2. Button heights 50/41px overriding the handover's 52/40px, which ships in `sizes.ts` in this same commit.
3. `letterSpacing: '0.02em'` in two files overriding the design system's `0px`, which ships in `typography.ts` in this same commit.

A reference implementation that contradicts the reference is worse than no reference. As-is these have **negative** value for the stated goal; fixed, they'd rank just behind the stories.

---

## Bottom line

Of the 901 out-of-scope lines, roughly **470 directly serve the goal** — `theme/index.ts`'s collision warning, the three stories, the font wiring, the collision guards, and the font-rename warning. Those aren't padding around the tokens; two of them are the difference between shipping token *data* and shipping a token *system* a team can build against.

Roughly **90 lines are pure overhead** (#11–14) — carried because the tooling demands it, contributing nothing.

The remaining **39 lines** (#15–17) are the ones to actually decide on. My recommendation: fix the three anti-patterns and keep them as the worked examples they're meant to be, or pull them into a follow-up PR. Merging them unchanged sets "the prototype beats the design system" as the house default on the very first day of FED build — which undercuts the thing the rest of the PR exists to establish.

content.text:
# Direct answer: mostly technicalities — and one of them was my own framing

Here's the honest accounting of *why* each item got flagged:

| Flagged because... | Items | Legitimate? |
|---|---|---|
| **My categorisation** — I defined "master design files" as the 8 foundation files + fonts, so everything else fell out by construction | Wiring (#1–4), stories (#5–7), tests (#8) | ❌ No merit. Artifact of my slicing |
| **A procedural technicality** — escalates the CODEOWNERS review path | Rules + derived files (#9–13) | ⚠️ Technicality. Fine on merit |
| **Genuine noise** | Registry (#14) | ✅ Real, but 4 lines |
| **A genuine defect** | Component retrofits (#15–17) | ✅ Real — but I prescribed the wrong fix |

Only **one** item in that list of 17 was flagged for a substantive reason. Let me replace the label with the real test.

## What actually happens if you remove it

| Item | Removable? | Consequence |
|---|---|---|
| **theme/index.ts** hunks | **No** | 5 functional lines. One of them is `styles: { global: globalStyles }` — remove it and **all 413 lines of `globalStyles.ts` become dead code.** `borderWidths` unregisters |
| **foundation/index.ts** hunks | **No** | The barrel export for `borderWidths`, `iconSizes`, `actionSizes`, `motion`, `zimmTokens`, `FONT_SERIF`. Without it the new foundation files aren't reachable through the public import surface |
| **_app-config** hunks | **No** | Brand typeface never loads; all 122 CSS vars undefined → the 36 `.zimm-*` classes render nothing |
| **vendor.d.ts** | **No** | `tsc --noEmit` fails → CI red |
| **3 stories** | Yes | Nothing breaks. You lose the browsable reference |
| **index.test.tsx** | Yes | Nothing breaks. You lose the collision tripwire |
| **rules files** | Yes | Nothing breaks. 3 new Tier 1 files + the fonts folder go unrecorded |
| **.cursor / copilot** | Only alongside the rules files | Orphaned, `sync:ai-rules:check` fails |
| **registry** | Futile | Pre-commit hook re-stages it on the next commit touching `components/` |
| **3 component retrofits** | Yes | Components revert to hardcoded hex. Design system lands with **zero consumers** |

**4 of the 17 are structurally mandatory** — they are the load-bearing wiring, not adjacent to the design system but the thing that makes it exist. Calling `theme/index.ts` "out of scope" when 3 of its lines are what activate 413 lines of core design system was a bad call on my part.

**1 is futile to remove.** The other 12 are removable, and removing 11 of them makes the deliverable worse, not tighter.

## What's genuinely unnecessary

Stripping it right down, out of 901 lines:

- **4 lines** of registry churn — auto-generated, can't be prevented, ignore it.
- **2 values** — not files, individual values — in the component retrofits: button heights `50/41px` vs the handover's `52/40px`, and `letterSpacing: '0.02em'` vs the design system's `0px`.

That's it. Everything else either has to be there or earns its place.

## Correcting my earlier recommendation

I said to split the three component files into a follow-up "so the foundation PR is purely the foundation." That was scope-purism and it's wrong.

Remove them and `develop` receives ~850 lines of token data with **nothing consuming it** and no demonstration that the substitution pattern works on a real component. Those three files are the only integration proof in the PR — they're what shows `action.primary.bgPressed` actually resolves where a hardcoded `#454545` used to sit. That's more valuable than a clean-looking diff.

The fix is to **correct the two values, keep the files.** Same for the `var(--zimm-*)` anti-pattern inside them — that's one architectural fix (moving var injection into the theme), not a reason to delete worked examples.

## Where that leaves you

Nothing in this branch needs to come out. The work to do before merge is three things, none of which is a removal:

1. **Fix the var-injection boundary** — spans `theme/index.ts` + `_app-config`. This is the only real defect, and it's what makes the stories trustworthy and the retrofits safe to copy.
2. **Resolve the two contradicting values** with the designer (plus the a11y contrast items from the first pass).
3. **Update `architecture.md` and `projectState.md`**, which were missed.

The 51% figure I led with was accurate as a measurement and misleading as an implication. A design system is roughly half tokens and half the wiring, reference, and proof that make tokens usable — that ratio is what a healthy foundation PR looks like, not scope creep.

=== 05-handover/platform/web/README.md ===
# Platform Base Layer: Web

**Current reference:** Baseline 2024 (widely available), WCAG 2.2
**Auto-check:** The `/extract-specs` skill prompts for target browsers and WCAG level if not set in `project.config.js`, and flags any design patterns that require degradation for the stated targets.

This file is shared infrastructure owned by the project lead. Do not edit it while working on an individual prototype or spec.

---

## Key platform constraints for designers

- There is no single viewport. Design must communicate breakpoints explicitly. Minimum: mobile (360px), tablet (768px), desktop (1280px). Note any others in the spec.
- No system-level gestures. Swipe interactions must be explicitly implemented and must have a non-gesture equivalent (button, keyboard).
- Animations must respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Every animation needs a fallback.
- Focus states are mandatory. Do not rely on browser defaults. Design explicit focus rings for interactive elements.
- Minimum touch target for pointer/touch dual-use surfaces: 44x44px.
- Custom fonts require FOUT/FOIT handling. Specify `font-display` strategy in the spec.

---

## Responsive breakpoints (default)

| Name | Min width | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Mobile | 360px | Default, designed first |
| Tablet | 768px | |
| Desktop | 1280px | |
| Wide | 1440px | Optional |

Override in the spec if the project uses different breakpoints.

---

## Browser degradation

Set target browsers in `project.config.js`. The `/extract-specs` skill flags any CSS or JS used in a prototype that is not supported by the stated targets and prompts the designer to note a fallback.

Common degradation patterns to anticipate:

| Feature | Baseline | Fallback |
|---|---|---|
| Container queries | Baseline 2023 | Media queries |
| `@layer` | Baseline 2022 | Manual specificity |
| `:has()` | Baseline 2023 | JS class toggle |
| View Transitions API | Partial | CSS transition fallback |
| `color-mix()` | Baseline 2023 | Static colour value |

---

## Accessibility (web)

- Screen readers: all interactive elements need a discernible name (`aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or visible text).
- Keyboard navigation: all interactions must be operable by keyboard. Tab order must be logical.
- Contrast: set WCAG level in `project.config.js` (AA or AAA). The extraction skill will flag failures.
- Reduce Motion: `@media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)` block required for all animations.
- Semantic HTML: use the correct element for the job (`button` not `div`, `nav` not `div`, etc.).

---

## Token naming conventions for web specs

Web specs use CSS custom properties directly from `02-design/library/common.css`. No mapping required. Reference tokens by their CSS variable name in the spec.

content.text:
Both branches are local now (`f2r-component-registry`, `f2r-implementation-workflow`). They change the picture substantially — including one item I'd treat as a stop-ship.

# What the F2R branches tell us

## 1. `f2r-implementation-workflow` is the same payload as your branch's first commit

Byte-identical shasums across all 9 theme files:

```
SAME  foundation/{colour,fonts,index,motion,sizes,typography,zimmTokens}.ts
SAME  theme/globalStyles.ts
SAME  theme/index.ts
```

`f2r-implementation-workflow` (e2ff84b, Jersey Perez, 11 Aug) == `design-tokens` commit `6c608b1` exactly. Same author. Your branch is that commit **plus two commits of refinement**, plus the fonts, `_app-config` wiring, 336 lines of tests and 3 stories.

**So the design-tokens branch strictly supersedes it — with one exception.** `f2r-implementation-workflow` carries **30 SVGs your branch does not have**: 28 icons + 2 logos under `overrides/app/static/img/ui-kits/`. Those are foundational design assets by your own definition, and they're currently only on the branch that's otherwise redundant.

Both target `develop`, both are 0 behind. Merging both would conflict on all 9 theme files. That needs a decision, not a merge order.

## 2. `f2r-component-registry` contains the source of truth I couldn't find

Earlier I flagged that the branch's comments reference a "Handover" (`tokens/colors.css`, `tokens.md`, `contract/zimm-contract.js`) that exists nowhere in the repo. It's all here:

```
f2r/02-design/library/tokens/{colors,typography,spacing,buttons,form-fields}.css
f2r/02-design/library/common.css
f2r/02-design/library/tokens.md          ← auto-extracted, with Figma node IDs + changelog
f2r/02-design/library/contract/zimm-contract.js
f2r/02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs
f2r/02-design/specs/components/*.md      ← 17 component specs
```

That closes the traceability gap. It also lets me check every open item against the actual source.

## 3. What the source resolves

| My earlier finding | What the handover actually says | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `text.inverseGrey` — `#969696` vs `#939393` contradiction | `colors.css:42` marks `#969696` **"confirmed"**, traced to `brand/color/palette/natural/300`. `tokens.md` is the auto-extracted file (`managed-by: /extract`) that *raised* the flag; `colors.css` carries the answer | **Branch is correct. Close this** |
| Motion tokens marked PROVISIONAL | `common.css:21-25`: *"Motion: PLACEHOLDER — All values provisional... Do not treat as final"* | **Branch faithfully mirrors source.** Genuinely open upstream, not a branch defect |
| Button heights 50/41 vs handover 52/40 | `buttons.css` + `button.md`: *"Height and padding driven by tokens mapped from `size` attribute"* | Handover is unambiguous. The prototype override is the deviation |
| Nav `letterSpacing: 0.02em` vs `0px` | `nav-item.md` maps link text to `--zimm-font-letterspacing-sm` (= `0px`) | Handover is unambiguous. `0.02em` has no handover basis |

Two of my four flags dissolve. The other two now have an in-repo, versioned source contradicting them — which matters, because `architecture.md:146` already states the prototype is *"AI-generated and desktop-only — also not a signed-off final design."* Keeping prototype values now means preferring the explicitly-unsigned source over the extracted design system.

## 4. New finding: the branch dropped a specified accessibility feature

I flagged that focus becomes invisible on dark backgrounds (`#191919` ring on `#191919` = 1.00:1). I attributed that to the design system. It isn't — `button.md:103` specifies it correctly:

> Focus ring: `var(--zimm-border-width-default) solid var(--zimm-color-border-focus)` (light) **or `var(--zimm-color-grey-white)` (inverse)**, offset 2px (primary) or 3px (secondary, accounts for 1px border)

The handover has a full inverse mode — `zimm-button` has an `inverse` attribute, and `--zimm-color-grey-white` is mapped to "focus ring (inverse)."

The branch collapsed this into a single composite token, `--zimm-focus-ring: '1px solid #191919'`, which hardcodes the light-mode colour and makes the inverse variant impossible to express. It also flattens the 2px/3px offset distinction to a flat 2px. **That's a port omission, and it's the fix for a real WCAG 2.4.7 failure.**

---

## 5. Stop-ship: the two branches contradict each other on font licensing

`f2r/.gitignore`:

```
# Monotype Desktop EULA prohibits server installation / redistribution
02-design/library/assets/Font Futura OTF/
02-design/library/assets/Font Futura WOFF2/
```

`tokens.md:358`: *"Futura Round is a licensed typeface and cannot be loaded from a public CDN. The consuming app must provide a `@font-face` declaration **or a licensed font service URL**."*

Meanwhile `feature/design-tokens-implementation-to-dev` commits **10 Futura Round `.woff2` files (336 KB)** into `overrides/app/static/fonts/` and serves them from Managed Runtime — which is server installation and redistribution. The only licence statement anywhere on the PWA side is a bare comment at `fonts.ts:1`: *"Futura Round: licensed, self-hosted."* No licence file, no EULA reference, nothing in `.docs/`.

I can't resolve this — I don't know what licence Zimmermann holds, and I couldn't read the font's embedded metadata (no brotli locally to decompress the woff2 name table). What I can state factually: **two people on your team took opposite positions on the same font files in the same week, and one of them wrote down a specific legal reason.** If the only licence in play is the Desktop EULA that Han Lee cited, committing these to a production storefront repo is a redistribution problem, and it's much cheaper to answer now than after it's in `develop` and deployed.

This needs someone with the actual licence documentation, before merge.

## 6. Governance note on `f2r-component-registry`

It modifies **`AGENTS.md`** (adds Hard Rule #16: *"When working on any file inside `f2r/`, disregard all rules in this file. Follow only `f2r/CLAUDE.md`."*) and touches root `package-lock.json` (+515). AGENTS.md is the one file AGENTS.md itself says needs both squad leads *and* the Integration lead — explicitly stronger than the verified-session Tier 1 exception. That's a heavier review path than the design-tokens branch faces.

## 7. One thing it does *not* solve

`contract/validate.mjs` validates the contract against `demo.html` files for Custom Elements (`<zimm-button>`). The specs say `**Stack:** web, react` and `**Status:** draft`, but the contract layer is web-components, not Chakra. **It does not validate your React theme** — so it doesn't replace `index.test.tsx`. The 336 lines still earn their place.

---

## What I'd do with this

1. **Answer the font licence question first.** Everything else is reversible; this one isn't, once it's deployed.
2. **Reconcile the three deviations against the now-in-repo handover** — button heights, nav letter-spacing, and the missing inverse focus ring. The first two are judgement calls that just got much easier; the third is a straight bug fix.
3. **Decide the duplication.** My read: fold `f2r-implementation-workflow`'s 30 icon/logo SVGs into the design-tokens branch and close it, rather than merging two branches that share 9 identical files. But that's a call for you and Jersey.
4. **Close the two flags that dissolved** — `inverseGrey` and motion. Both were correct as shipped, and the branch's comments should be updated to cite `f2r/02-design/library/` now that it's in-repo rather than describing it as an external unresolved contradiction.

Want me to run the same comparison the other direction — check whether anything in the handover's 36 `.zimm-*` classes or 122 tokens was *dropped* in the port to `globalStyles.ts`/`zimmTokens.ts`?

# Blocker 1 — Futura Round licensing

## What's actually happening

`getAssetUrl()` resolves to `window.Progressive.buildOrigin` — the public MRT bundle CDN. So the 10 `.woff2` files in `overrides/app/static/fonts/` get published to a **public, unauthenticated CDN** on every deploy. That is precisely "server installation and redistribution."

Two positions in your repo, same week, same font family:

| | Position | Stated reason |
|---|---|---|
| **Han** — `f2r/.gitignore` | Excluded from git | *"Monotype Desktop EULA prohibits server installation / redistribution"* |
| **Jersey** — `overrides/app/static/fonts/` | 10 files committed + CDN-served | `fonts.ts:1` comment: *"licensed, self-hosted"* — no licence doc anywhere in repo |

And Han's own handover tells you which side it expects (`tokens.md:358`):

> Futura Round is a licensed typeface and cannot be loaded from a public CDN. The consuming app must provide a `@font-face` declaration **or a licensed font service URL**.

That sentence is doing a lot of work. It hands the licensing decision to you — it doesn't assert you're covered.

## Something you can fix regardless of the answer

The design system uses **weights 400 and 500 only**. Its only italic style (`textStyles.serif`) uses Source Serif 4, not Futura oblique.

```
USED   (Regular 400 + Medium 500)    60,148 bytes   2 files
UNUSED                              261,320 bytes   8 files   ← 81% of the payload
```

Light, LightOblique, Medium**Oblique**, Demi, DemiOblique, Bold, BoldOblique, Oblique — all committed, all CDN-published, **referenced by nothing.** `_app-config` declares `@font-face` for all ten, so they're not unreachable either: anyone writing `fontWeight="700"` would silently pull an unintended weight down.

That's 8 files of pure licence exposure with zero rendering benefit. True in every branch of the decision tree below.

## Your decision tree

**Ask: does Zimmermann hold a Webfont (self-hosting) licence for Futura Round, or only a Desktop licence?**

**→ Webfont licence exists.** You're fine. Keep the 2 used files, drop the other 8, and put the licence reference in `fonts.ts` next to the "licensed, self-hosted" claim so the next person doesn't have to re-litigate this. Check whether it's domain-scoped — you have 8 storefronts across 6 regions.

**→ Only a Desktop licence** (what Han cited). Self-hosting is a breach and needs to come out before this reaches `develop`. Options, cheapest first:
1. Ship the branch with the fallback stack already in `fonts.ts` (Century Gothic → Gill Sans → Trebuchet). Costs you brand fidelity, costs nothing legally, unblocks everything else in the branch today.
2. Monotype's hosted web font service — the `licensed font service URL` route the handover names.
3. Procure a Webfont licence, then re-add.

**→ Nobody knows.** Treat it as Desktop-only and take option 1. The branch's other ~1,400 lines don't depend on the fonts.

## Who to ask

Han first — they cited the specific EULA, so they've either seen the licence or know who holds it. Then whoever procured the typeface on Zimmermann's side (brand/design, possibly via the SOW). This isn't a call you or I can make from the repo; there's no licence artifact in it to read, and I couldn't read the font's embedded metadata either (no brotli locally to decompress the name table).

## What I'd do next

Nothing to the fonts until you have the answer — and per repo rules I won't delete files without you asking.

But I can prep the no-regrets change now: strip the 8 unused `.woff2` and their 8 `@font-face` blocks, leaving Regular + Medium. That shrinks the exposure to the two weights you actually render and is correct under every outcome above.

Want me to prep that, or hold everything on fonts and move to **Blocker 2 — the `var(--zimm-*)` resolution boundary** (the one that makes Storybook and the new Foundation stories render wrong)?

# Net effect of removing the fonts

## Code impact: small and fully contained

The font wiring touches exactly **one file** plus the assets. Nothing else in the repo depends on it.

| What goes | Where |
|---|---|
| 10 `.woff2` (321 KB) | `overrides/app/static/fonts/` |
| `FuturaFontFaces()` — 10 `@font-face` blocks | `_app-config` lines 133–213 |
| `FuturaFontPreload()` | `_app-config` lines 108–131 |
| 2 JSX usages | `_app-config` lines 278–279 |
| `import Helmet` + `import { getAssetUrl }` | `_app-config` lines 9, 11 — **used for nothing else** |
| Their two `vendor.d.ts` shims | Become dead (harmless if left) |

~106 lines out of one file. That's it.

**What does *not* break:**
- `tsc --noEmit` — clean. `fonts.ts` still exports the same strings.
- **All 143 tests still pass.** The font test asserts `theme.fonts.body` *contains* `'Futura Round'` — a string check on the stack, never a file check.
- Lint, build, the 122 `--zimm-*` tokens, 36 `.zimm-*` classes, colours, spacing, sizes, motion — all untouched.

**Docs that go stale** (need updating in the same change): `fonts.ts:1-3`, `zimmTokens.ts:92-97`, `frozenFiles.md` (the `static/fonts/` Tier 1 entry this branch *added*, plus its 2 derived copies via `npm run sync:ai-rules`), and `typography.stories.tsx:13` which currently says *"This story doubles as the visual check that Futura Round actually loaded."*

## Performance: actually improves

- −2 preload requests / −60 KB off the critical path
- −321 KB from the bundle
- No FOUT/swap flash at all
- Your ≤2s p75 mobile LCP budget gets **easier**, not harder

## Visual impact: this is the real cost

Fallback chain is `Futura Round → Futura LT Pro → Futura → Century Gothic → Gill Sans → Trebuchet MS → Arial → sans-serif`. With no `@font-face`, the first three only resolve if the font is **installed locally**. So:

| Platform | Renders as | Distance from Futura |
|---|---|---|
| Windows + Office | Century Gothic | Close — geometric |
| macOS | Gill Sans | Noticeably off — humanist, not geometric |
| **iOS** | Trebuchet MS | Far |
| **Android** | Roboto | Far |

Mobile — your priority platform — lands on the two worst matches.

### ⚠️ The trap you need to know about

**The people reviewing the UI are the most likely to have Futura Round installed.** Han's team holds the Desktop licence — that's the whole basis for the EULA concern. So designers, and any FED dev who installs it locally, will see correct Futura Round in the browser while **customers see Trebuchet/Roboto.**

That's a silent dev≠prod divergence in the most visible design element on the site. If you take this path, it needs to be stated loudly, or someone will sign off on a design review that doesn't reflect production.

This also kills the tempting middle option — gitignore the fonts but keep them locally so devs see the "real" thing. Don't. It institutionalises exactly that divergence.

### Second-order: your pixel baseline goes away

The type scale hardcodes px line-heights and **negative letter-spacing** (`-0.12px`, `-0.14px`) tuned to Futura Round's wide geometric forms. A substituted face changes advance widths, x-height and cap-height, so:

- Text occupies different widths → wrapping and truncation risk in the nav, `minWidth: 80px` buttons, product tiles
- Negative tracking tuned for Futura may read cramped on Trebuchet/Roboto
- Fixed line-heights against a different x-height shifts vertical rhythm

For the FED build that's a **process cost, not a code cost**: devs comparing against Figma won't know whether a mismatch is their bug or the font substitution. You'd want to say that explicitly in the PR and in whatever QA baseline you set.

## Where that leaves the decision

Removal is technically cheap and legally clean. The cost is entirely brand fidelity — and it's **not really yours to absorb alone.** Taking Han's stance means the storefront doesn't render in the brand typeface at go-live unless a Webfont licence is procured. Brand/design should know that before it becomes a fait accompli in `develop`.

My read: your instinct is right on the legal question — a written EULA citation beats an undocumented "licensed, self-hosted" comment, and merging the risky version into `develop` is the expensive mistake. But I'd split it into two decisions:

1. **Now, low-regret:** drop the 8 unused weights (261 KB, 81% of the payload, referenced by nothing). Correct under every outcome.
2. **Escalate:** the remaining 2 weights are a brand + procurement call, not a code call. A Monotype Webfont licence for 2 weights is a small, well-understood purchase — worth pricing before you commit to shipping in Trebuchet.

# Tier 1 — Frozen Files

These files must not be modified by Claude Code without the developer explicitly naming the file
in the prompt AND confirming they have spoken to the listed owner. No exceptions.

> **Note:** this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — paths
> below reference `overrides/app/...` (the customisation surface) rather than the upstream
> monorepo `packages/template-retail-react-app/app/...` path.

## Design System (Owner: UI Designer — #design-system)

The whole `overrides/app/theme/foundation/` folder is Tier 1. Currently present:

```text
overrides/app/theme/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/index.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/colour.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/fonts.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/typography.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/gridSystem.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/spacing.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/motion.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/sizes.ts
overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens.ts
overrides/app/static/fonts/
```

`static/fonts/` holds the licensed Futura Round `.woff2` files. They are the payload that
`foundation/fonts.ts` resolves to, and `_app-config/index.tsx` maps all ten filenames across
weights 300–700 — so renaming or deleting one silently drops that weight to the fallback
stack with no build error and no failing test. Same owner as the tokens that reference them.

Per-component theme overrides live in `overrides/app/theme/components/` and are
**Tier 2** — see [protectedFiles.md](./protectedFiles.md). `overrides/app/theme/globalStyles.ts`
is also **Tier 2** — it composes the `.zimm-*` global class registry from the `--zimm-*`
variables defined in `foundation/zimmTokens.ts`, so it is derived styling rather than a
brand token source, but it emits CSS on every page and therefore needs a named owner.

## Commerce SDK Hooks (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-basket.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-current-customer.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-einstein.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-datacloud.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-refresh-token.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-multi-site.ts
overrides/app/hooks/use-navigation.ts
```

Note: `commerce-sdk-react` is consumed from `node_modules/@salesforce/commerce-sdk-react/` —
it is not in this repo and cannot be modified here. The hooks above are the overrides surface.

## Runtime & Integration Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
config/                              ← entire directory (default.js, sites.js, sit.js, dev.js, utils.js)
overrides/app/ssr.js
overrides/app/ssr/                   ← SSR helper modules split from ssr.js in refactor 610020e:
                                         connectionPools.ts  — undici pool isolation (blast-radius mitigation)
                                         contentSecurityPolicy.ts  — CSP headers; wrong change = security hole on every page
                                         slasTokens.ts  — SLAS auth token handling; wrong change = broken auth site-wide
                                         paymentMetadata.ts  — payment method metadata SSR (checkout pages)
                                         marketingCloud.ts  — MC client-credentials token exchange
worker/main.js
package.json (root)
mobify.config.js
overrides/app/config/countries.ts
overrides/app/config/contentful.ts   ← gates preview/draft content; removing the server-side check exposes drafts on production
```

**`overrides/app/request-processor.js` — add here when populated.**
Currently the Salesforce example stub. Once Zimmermann's geo-redirect and storefront-routing logic lands here it runs on every single request — it will be one of the highest-blast-radius files in the repo. Add it to this section before that work begins.

## Build Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Path aliases are configured in four places that must stay in sync (see architecture.md §Path Aliases).
Breaking either file silently breaks every `app/` and `~` import across the codebase.

```text
babel.config.js    ← path aliases for npm start dev server + production build
tsconfig.json      ← path aliases for TypeScript / VS Code intellisense; also enforces strict mode
```

## Consent (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
Didomi / consent configuration (paths TBD — add when introduced)
```

## Test & Tooling Config (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

Mirrors AGENTS.md hard rule 8 — test config drift breaks every contributor's harness.

```text
vitest.config.*
vitest.setup.ts       ← test environment setup; complements vitest.config.*
playwright.config.*
.storybook/
lighthouserc.js
.browserstack.yml     ← must target e2e/tests/zimm only; scope change = CI cost explosion + upstream test failures
```

## CI/CD Pipeline (Owner: Integration / SI Partner — #integration)

```text
.github/workflows/
```

## Governance (Owner: Both Squad Leads + Integration Lead — #dev-team)

```text
AGENTS.md
CLAUDE.md
CODEOWNERS
.claude/rules/
.claude/settings.json
coderabbit.yaml              ← AI PR review config; weakening it removes Tier 1 change detection and commit-format enforcement
.coderabbit/                 ← ast-grep rule content coderabbit.yaml points at; weakening/deleting a rule here silently removes that check with no signal in coderabbit.yaml itself
semgrep.yml                  ← semgrep rule content (payment-credential-logging, XSS); same silent-weakening risk as .coderabbit/
scripts/hooks/pre-commit     ← enforces Contentful drift check and blocks direct edits to derived AI config files
scripts/hooks/commit-msg     ← enforces conventional commits; /generate-changelog depends on this
```
