content.text:
Verified: this repo merges via **merge commits** (every merge into `develop` has two parents), not squash. That's the fact that decides this. Here's the plain version.

## The one idea: git never forgets, it only adds

Git doesn't store "the current files." It stores a **snapshot at every commit**, forever. Each of your 3 commits saved a snapshot that *contains* the 10 font files.

A new "delete the fonts" commit doesn't erase them — it adds a **4th snapshot** that happens to not have them. The first 3 snapshots still do, and anyone can pull the fonts back out:

```
git show 6c608b1:overrides/app/static/fonts/FuturaRound-Regular.woff2   → the font, intact
```

**Analogy:** it's a photo album where you can only ever add pages, never tear one out. Adding a page captioned "the fonts are gone now" doesn't remove the earlier pages that still show them.

## Why that matters *here* specifically

I checked how your PRs land: **merge commits**. When this branch merges, all 3 of its commits become permanent parts of `develop`'s history — font snapshots included.

```
your branch:   6c608b1 ──→ 5561356 ──→ 95c9df9 ──→ [my delete commit]
               [fonts]     [fonts]     [fonts]      [no fonts]
                  └────────────┴────────────┴──── still there, forever, on GitHub
                                                    and inherited by develop on merge
```

So the licence says *"no copy on any server"* — and a plain commit leaves 3 copies sitting in GitHub's history on a server. The files stop *shipping to customers* (they're gone from the build), but they're not *gone*.

## Your three options

| Option | What it does | Fonts in history? | Cost |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Plain commit** (what's staged) | Adds the 4th snapshot on top | **Yes** — in all 3 old commits + inherited by develop | Zero. Honest audit trail: "added, then removed" |
| **B. Squash** | Collapses all 4 commits into **one** clean commit with no fonts ever | **No** | Loses the 3-commit granularity; force-push needed |
| **C. History rewrite** | Surgically strips the blobs from the 3 commits, keeps the commit structure | **No** | Most complex; force-push; Jersey must re-clone |

**Note:** GitHub's own "Squash and merge" button at PR time would *also* strip them from `develop` — but your repo uses merge commits, so you can't rely on that; it has to be done to the branch first (B or C).

## What I'd recommend

**B (squash).** Reasoning:

- The 3 commits are all unmerged work-in-progress on one feature branch — there's no external history depending on their individual boundaries, so collapsing them costs you nothing real.
- It's far simpler and less error-prone than C, and gets the identical result: `develop` never sees the blobs.
- The only "loss" is granularity that only matters if someone needed to bisect *within* this branch's font evolution — which, given we're deleting the fonts entirely, nobody will.

The single squashed commit uses the message I already drafted.

**The honest caveat:** even after B, the *old* commits still exist on the GitHub branch ref until the branch is deleted and GitHub garbage-collects (and truly purging a public fork/cache needs a GitHub support request). But squashing before merge is the standard, defensible bar — it keeps them out of `develop`, which is the mainline everyone builds from. Full forensic erasure is a different, heavier conversation and probably overkill for an internal repo where the fix is caught pre-merge.

One decision from you: **A, B, or C.** If B, I'll also want your explicit go to force-push the branch (rewrites shared history — Hard Rule #15 territory).

But `colour.ts` isn't in our font change, and fixing it means editing a **Tier 1 token value** → belongs to Phase 2 with the designer, not smuggled into a font-scoped commit. Leaving it, as planned.
- **#1 and #3 (Tier 1 "get designer approval")** are process assertions, not code bugs. CodeRabbit doesn't know these foundation files *are* the F2R designer handover, or that this is a verified tier-1-approver session (your `gh` login is in `tier-1-approvers`). Per AGENTS.md these get an in-thread reply on the PR, not a code change.

**Nothing here blocks or is caused by the font removal.** CodeRabbit didn't flag a single one of our actual edits (the deletions, `_app-config`, `fonts.ts`, `vendor.d.ts`, governance). Review requirement satisfied.

Option B collapses **all commits into one**. That means the squashed commit contains the *entire* design-tokens feature, not just the font removal — so the `fix(theme)` font-only message I drafted would be **inaccurate**. A whole-feature squash is a `feat(theme)`. Here's the corrected message:

properties behind the .zimm-* global classes, both ported 1:1 from the F2R
Handover design library. Fonts are the one deliberate exception — see below.

  borderWidths and the zimmTokens --zimm-* registry (Tier 1)

content.text:
`fe04791` — here's exactly what it was.

## What it is
A **squash of the whole branch into one commit** (the 3 originals `6c608b1`/`5561356`/`95c9df9` collapsed into 1), sitting directly on `develop`. 24 files, +1638/−89.

## It had two purposes at once

**1. Mechanical (the reason for squashing):** get the 10 licensed Futura Round `.woff2` blobs out of the branch's *history*, not just its tip — so they never ride into `develop` on merge. That was **Blocker #1**, and squashing was the agreed way (Option B) to achieve it, since a plain deletion commit would've left the blobs in the three old commits.

**2. Content (what the commit actually delivers):** the full **Zimmermann design-token foundation** — the F2R Handover design system landed as two synchronised surfaces:
- Chakra scales — `colour`, `typography` (22 text styles), `spacing`, `sizes`, `motion`, `borderWidths`
- the `--zimm-*` CSS custom-property registry + 36 `.zimm-*` global classes
- component overrides swapping hardcoded literals for tokens (`button`, `header`, `listMenu`)
- 3 Foundation Storybook stories + 143 cross-surface tests
- governance updates (Tier 1 lists, EULA record)

## The font decision, folded in
The commit's headline exception: **Futura Round is *not* self-hosted** — Monotype Desktop EULA forbids serving the files, so no `.woff2` are committed and type renders from the Century Gothic / Gill Sans fallback stack. That's the resolution of Blocker #1, baked into the same commit.

## What it deliberately did *not* touch
The 5 Phase 2 items — inverse focus ring, `var(--zimm-*)` Storybook resolution, contrast failures, prototype-vs-Handover deviations, and doc drift. All left for follow-up, all still open (the status I just gave you).

**In one line:** it brought the design-token foundation onto the branch cleanly while stripping the licence-violating fonts from history — the token system minus the fonts, as a single squashed commit.

One caveat I'd restate honestly: because it's a squash of the entire branch, that single commit now represents *all* the token work, not just the font fix — so its scope is "the whole feature," and the font handling is the notable exception within it, not the entirety of it.

Good scope-discipline question. The branch's stated intent — from the top — is: **land the master/foundational design files from the F2R handover, faithfully, to guide the FED build that's commencing.** Measuring each item against *that*:

| # | Item | Aligned with branch intent? | In scope for *this* branch? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Inverse focus ring | ✅ Yes — the handover *specifies* it (`button.md:103`), the branch dropped it | ✅ In scope — it's a **fidelity gap**, an incomplete port |
| 2 | `var(--zimm-*)` Storybook resolution | ✅ Yes — the foundation renders *wrong* in the very tool the FED build references | ✅ In scope — the deliverable isn't functional without it |
| 3 | Contrast failures | ⚠️ Aligned with the *project's* WCAG AA mandate, but **not** with "land the handover faithfully" | ❌ Out — this is a **design change**, not a port |
| 4 | Prototype-vs-Handover deviations | ✅ Yes — branch diverged from the master source | ✅ In scope — another **fidelity gap** |
| 5 | Doc drift | ✅ Yes — keeps the repo's record of the delivered foundation accurate | ✅ In scope — housekeeping for this deliverable |

## The distinction that matters

**Four of the five make the foundation you're delivering *correct*:**
- #1 and #4 are **port-fidelity fixes** — the branch didn't match its own source (the handover / Han's specs). Correcting them is finishing the job the branch exists to do, not new work.
- #2 makes the foundation **actually usable** in Storybook — which is the point of landing it "to guide the FED build."
- #5 keeps the **records honest** about what landed.

These are all "complete the deliverable faithfully" → squarely in scope.

**#3 is the odd one out.** The contrast failures are in the handover values *themselves* (`#969696` hover = 2.96:1). Fixing them means **overriding the designer's design**, not faithfully porting it. That's aligned with the project's accessibility goal, but it's a *design decision* that belongs to the designer — possibly fixed in Figma and re-handed-over. Treating it as "part of this branch" would have us silently changing brand tokens, which Hard Rule #3 explicitly forbids.

## So, practically

- **On this branch:** #2 (I can implement once you pick approach a/b) and #5 (I can do now). These need no design input and complete the deliverable.
- **On this branch, but designer-gated:** #1 and #4 — in scope as fidelity fixes, but they touch Tier 1 foundation, so they need the designer's nod. Fast, because the handover already dictates the values (apply, don't invent).
- **Not this branch — hand to the designer:** #3. It's a genuine design change; surface it, don't absorb it.

Net: **4 of 5 belong to this branch's mission; #3 is adjacent** — right for the project, wrong to fold into a "faithfully land the handover" branch without the designer deciding.

Want me to proceed with the two ungated ones (#5 now, #2 on your a/b pick) and draft the designer note covering #1, #3, #4?

content.text:
The verification changed my answer on #2, so I need to correct something I told you earlier before showing the states.

**Correction:** I called #2 "critical — the Foundation stories render blank." **That was wrong.** The evidence shows the 3 Foundation stories use *Chakra* tokens (`textStyle=`, `color=`, the JS objects), not the `.zimm-*` classes — so they render **correctly** in Storybook. The only `--zimm-*` consumer in the stories is one `.zimm-grid` demo (loses side-padding, keeps its columns). The real `--zimm-*` breakage lands on **component overrides** (button/header/listMenu, which use `var(--zimm-*)`) — and components are Han's domain.

That reframes #2. Here are both, current → fixed → why/what.

---

## #5 — Doc drift (clean, this branch's own record)

**Current — `architecture.md:136`:**
> brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, **fonts, typography, gridSystem, spacing** — Tier 1, UI Designer owned)

Missing `motion`, `sizes`, `zimmTokens`; no mention of `globalStyles`; still implies fonts ship here.

**Fixed:**
> brand tokens live in `foundation/` (colour, typography, gridSystem, spacing, sizes, motion, and the `--zimm-*` registry in `zimmTokens.ts` — Tier 1, UI Designer owned); the `.zimm-*` global classes composed from them live in `globalStyles.ts` (Tier 2). Note: brand fonts are **not** self-hosted (licence) — see `frozenFiles.md`.

**Current — `projectState.md:46`:**
> Design tokens **finalised** from Figma in `.../foundation/` (`colour.ts`, `fonts.ts`, `typography.ts`, `gridSystem.ts`, `spacing.ts`).

Stale file list; "finalised" contradicts the open designer items (#1/#3/#4); implies fonts present.

**Fixed:**
> Design token foundation ported from the F2R Handover into `.../foundation/` (colour, typography, spacing, sizes, motion, `zimmTokens`) + `.zimm-*` classes in `globalStyles.ts`, composed in `index.ts`. Fonts render from the fallback stack — Futura Round is **not** self-hosted (Monotype Desktop EULA). Open with UI designer: primary-hover contrast, inverse focus ring, button-height & nav letter-spacing deviations.

**Why/what:** `.docs/` isn't Tier 1; Han doesn't correct these. They describe the very foundation the manual builders read — stale/false descriptions mislead them. Pure factual catch-up, no code impact.

---

## #2 — `var(--zimm-*)` resolution

**Current state (accurate this time):**
- `--zimm-*` vars are injected **only** by `_app-config` (`<Global styles={zimmRootVarsCss}>`). Storybook mounts `<ChakraProvider theme>` without `_app-config` → vars undefined.
- **What actually breaks in Storybook:** component overrides using `var(--zimm-*)` (button ×7, listMenu ×9, header ×3 refs) render with unresolved font-sizes/borders; the `.zimm-*` global classes are inert. **What does *not* break:** the 3 Foundation stories (Chakra-token based) — only the lone `.zimm-grid` demo loses padding.

**Fixed state — and here's the constraint:** the obvious fix (move the `:root` block into the theme's `styles.global`) is **proven broken.** I just tested it: Chakra's processor mangled `'Futura Round', 'Century Gothic', sans-serif` down to `'Century Gothic'`. That's the documented reason the vars live in raw Emotion in `_app-config`. So the only working fix is a **Storybook decorator** injecting the same raw block:

```tsx
// .storybook/preview.tsx  (new decorator)
import { Global, css } from '@emotion/react';
import { zimmTokens } from '../overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens';
const zimmVars = css`:root { ${Object.entries(zimmTokens).map(([k,v])=>`${k}:${v}`).join(';')} }`;
const withZimmTokens: Decorator = (Story) => (<><Global styles={zimmVars} /><Story /></>);
// ...add to decorators
```

**Why I'm now recommending we DON'T do #2 on this branch:**

1. **It's not critical to this branch's goal.** The reference artifact — the Foundation stories — works. I was wrong earlier; the evidence corrects it.
2. **The fix is Integration's Tier 1 territory.** `.storybook/` is frozen test config (Hard Rule #8, Integration-owned). The theme-only route that would keep it in *our* files is proven broken by the font-mangling.
3. **Its main beneficiary is Han's component stories** — the thing that breaks is component-override rendering, which is Han's stream.

So #2 fails your own test: it's largely someone else's to own (Integration's config + Han's components), and it's not critical to the foundation this branch delivers.

---

## Revised recommendation

**Do only #5.** It's the sole item that is unambiguously this branch's, safe, and serves the manual builders.

**Defer #2** — but not silently: document it as a known limitation (`.zimm-*` classes and `var(--zimm-*)`-based overrides only resolve inside the app shell, not bare Storybook/test mounts) and hand it to Integration, since fixing it means touching their `.storybook` config and it chiefly unblocks Han's component work.

That leaves this branch as: `fe04791` + a small **#5-only** doc commit. Want me to do #5 and write the one-paragraph #2 limitation note for the handoff?

content.text:
All three new Foundation stories built successfully (Colour, Spacing, Typography — plus the pre-existing Icons). Artifacts cleaned, tree clean. Here's the full analysis and plan.

---

# Part 1 — Diff analysis: what's landing on `develop` and its risk

**26 files, +1640/−91.** No font binaries (never on `develop`). Classified by **blast radius** — the axis that matters for a theme change, because `_app-config` + `theme/` apply to *every page*.

| Risk | Files | Why it's risky | Runtime reach |
|---|---|---|---|
| **R1 — Global, highest** | `_app-config/index.tsx`, `theme/index.ts`, `foundation/{colour,typography,fonts}.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`, `globalStyles.ts` | The root provider + theme apply site-wide. A broken provider = white screen; a remapped scale silently restyles ~199 base call sites | Every page, every site |
| **R2 — Shared components** | `theme/components/{button,header,listMenu}.ts` | Buttons/nav are on nearly every page; the `var(--zimm-*)` refs here only resolve in-app | Most pages |
| **R3 — Additive foundation** | `foundation/{motion,sizes,spacing}.ts`, `foundation/index.ts` | New exports; risk only if consumed wrong. No current consumers | None until used |
| **R4 — Dev/test only** | 3 Foundation `*.stories.tsx`, `index.test.tsx` | No production bundle impact | Storybook/CI only |
| **R5 — Zero runtime** | `.claude/**`, `.cursor/**`, `.github/copilot-instructions.md`, `.docs/**`, `registry` | Governance/docs | None |

**The three genuine hazards this diff must be proven against:**
1. **Provider integrity** — `_app-config` is the app root; must still boot.
2. **Scale-collision** — Zimmermann `md/xs/2xs/3xs` font sizes collide with Chakra's, used at ~199 base sites. A remap = silent site-wide restyle.
3. **`--zimm-*` resolution gap (known, #2)** — the `.zimm-*` classes + component-override `var()` refs resolve **only in-app** (via `_app-config`), *not* in bare Storybook/test mounts.

---

# Part 2 — Testing plan (layered, mapped to repo infrastructure)

## ✅ Layer 0–3 — Already executed this session

| Layer | Tool | Result | Covers |
|---|---|---|---|
| Static types | `tsc --noEmit` | **PASS** (exit 0) | Compile integrity, R1–R3 |
| Unit + guards | `vitest run` | **PASS 143/143** | Scale-collision guard, `extendTheme` merge, textStyle end-to-end, Chakra↔`--zimm-*` agreement (hazard #2 caught here) |
| Lint | `pwa-kit-dev lint` | 22 problems — **all pre-existing**, none in the 26 diff files | Style, no new debt |
| Prod build | `pwa-kit-dev build` | **PASS** (exit 0) | Webpack/SSR compile, R1 provider bundles |
| Bundle budget | `bundlesize` | **PASS** — main 102.9/180 KB, vendor 515/550 KB gzip | Perf budget (LCP guardrail) |
| Storybook build | `build-storybook` | **PASS** — all 3 Foundation stories in index | R4 stories compile/render-build |

**That's every gate `qa.yml` + `digital-sit.yml` run automatically, and they're green.**

## ⏳ Layer 4–6 — Need a running server or your go (the gaps automation can't close)

A theme change is fundamentally *visual*, and this repo has **no visual-regression tool** (Chromatic/Loki are explicitly out of scope per `testing.md`). So pixels and in-app var resolution are **not** covered above. These three close that gap:

| # | Layer | How to run | Pass criteria | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **4** | **Storybook a11y + interaction** | `npm run storybook` (server) → `test-storybook --ci` | Stories render; a11y clean **except the known contrast fails (#3)** | Will surface #3's 2.96:1 — *expected*, not a new defect. Confirms nothing *else* regressed |
| **5** | **E2E regression** | dev server up → `npm run test:e2e` (localhost, homepage smoke + any specs) | Themed app still renders + navigates; no console errors | Proves hazard #1 (provider boots) on a real page. **Needs `npm start`** — which I'm not permitted to run; you'd start it |
| **6** | **Browser visual + in-app `--zimm-*`** | you start `npm start`; I drive Chrome | Home/PLP/PDP render in fallback font, no layout breakage; `getComputedStyle(:root)` shows `--zimm-*` **resolved** (proving hazard #2 is app-only, not app-broken) | The one that actually validates the theme *looks right* and the vars work in production context |

## Recommended execution order

1. **Layers 0–3: done, all green** ✅
2. **Layer 4** — I can run it now if you want (I'll start the Storybook server and test-runner), accepting the known #3 contrast flags as expected.
3. **Layers 5–6** — these need `npm start`. Per project rule I won't start it; **if you start the dev server**, I'll drive the browser to (a) confirm the app boots and key pages render, (b) prove `--zimm-*` resolves in-app, (c) eyeball the fallback-font rendering. This is the highest-value manual check for a theme PR.

## Explicit non-goals (out of scope for this branch, per earlier decisions)
- **#2 fix** (Storybook var injection) — Integration's `.storybook`; the plan *documents* the limitation rather than fixing it.
- **#1/#3/#4** (focus ring, contrast values, prototype deviations) — Han's components / UI designer. Layer 4 will *report* #3 but we don't fix it here.

---

**Verdict so far:** every automated gate that gates a merge is green, tree clean, no new lint, bundle within budget. The branch is mechanically sound. What remains before I'd call it "PR-ready with confidence" is the **visual/in-app layer (5–6)** — which needs the dev server.

Server stopped, tree clean. Here's the Layer 4 result and an important caveat about what it does and doesn't prove.

## Layer 4 — Storybook render + a11y: PASS

```
PASS  foundation/typography.stories.tsx
PASS  foundation/spacing.stories.tsx
PASS  foundation/colour.stories.tsx
PASS  components/icons/icons.stories.tsx
PASS  components/button/index.stories.tsx
Test Suites: 5 passed · Tests: 14 passed · 5.2s
```

**What this proves:**
- All 3 new Foundation stories **render in a real browser without runtime errors** — no theme-composition crash, no `extendTheme` blow-up, no ListMenu-style "undefined in theme" throw.
- **axe a11y ran** (addon-a11y, `test: 'error'`) and found **zero static violations** across the rendered content — Foundation, Icons, and Button.
- It confirms my earlier corrected finding on **#2**: the Foundation stories render fine *without* `--zimm-*` injection because they're Chakra-token based. So the deferred var-resolution gap does **not** break this branch's reference stories. Good, empirical confirmation.

## Caveat — what Layer 4 did NOT clear (be precise about this)

I earlier said Layer 4 would "surface the known contrast (#3)." **It didn't, and it can't** — here's why that's not a false all-clear:

- axe checks the **statically rendered DOM**. The #3 failure (2.96:1) is a `:hover` state — white text on `#969616` hover background. No story renders a button *in hover*, so axe never sees that pixel combination.
- The static states that *are* rendered (default button = black/white = 17:1) pass legitimately.

So **#3 remains an open, known item** — Layer 4 neither confirms nor refutes it. It's already quantified from my manual ratio analysis and correctly parked with the UI designer. I don't want the green check to read as "contrast is fine."

## Where we are on the plan

| Layer | Status |

| 0 Static (tsc) | ✅ |

| 1b Lint | ✅ (no new) |

content.text:
It's the handoff artifact — a short, self-contained write-up of the one known limitation we deliberately did **not** fix on this branch, so whoever picks it up (Integration owns `.storybook`; Han's component stories are the main beneficiary) has the full context and doesn't have to re-derive it. Here it is, ready to drop into the PR description or a Jira ticket:

---

### Known limitation: `--zimm-*` variables don't resolve outside the app shell

**What**
The `--zimm-*` CSS custom properties are injected onto `:root` by **`_app-config/index.tsx` only** (a raw Emotion `<Global>` block). Any harness that mounts the theme *without* `_app-config` — Storybook (`.storybook/preview.tsx` mounts a bare `<ChakraProvider theme>`) and bare `ChakraProvider` unit renders — does **not** get those vars. As a result, the 36 `.zimm-*` global classes and the component-override `var(--zimm-*)` references (button ×7, listMenu ×9, header ×3) render **unresolved** in Storybook. ~44 `var(--zimm-*)` references are affected in a bare mount.

**What is NOT affected**
- **The real app** — verified in-browser (all probed `--zimm-*` resolve on `:root` at `localhost:3000`). This is a harness gap, not a product defect.
- **The 3 Foundation stories** (`Foundation/Colour|Typography|Spacing`) — they use Chakra tokens (`textStyle=`, `color=`), not `.zimm-*` classes, so they render correctly. Confirmed: Storybook test-runner 14/14 pass.
- Impact is concentrated on **component stories** whose theme overrides consume `var(--zimm-*)` — i.e. Han's component work.

**Why it wasn't fixed here**
- The clean theme-side fix (emit the `:root` block from `theme/index.ts` `styles.global`) is **ruled out**: Chakra's style processor mangles font-family values — verified, `'Futura Round', 'Century Gothic', sans-serif` collapses to `'Century Gothic'`. That's the original reason the vars live in raw Emotion in `_app-config`.
- The only working fix touches **`.storybook/preview.tsx`**, which is **Tier 1 test config (Integration-owned, Hard Rule #8)** — out of scope for this feature branch.

**Recommended fix (for Integration)**
Add a decorator to `.storybook/preview.tsx` injecting the same raw block, reusing the existing token source:
```tsx
import { Global, css } from '@emotion/react';
import { zimmTokens } from '../overrides/app/theme/foundation/zimmTokens';
const zimmVars = css`:root { ${Object.entries(zimmTokens).map(([k,v]) => `${k}:${v}`).join(';')} }`;
const withZimmTokens: Decorator = (Story) => (<><Global styles={zimmVars} /><Story /></>);
// prepend to `decorators`
```
This mirrors exactly what `_app-config` does in the app, so Storybook renders identically to production. Optional follow-up: extract the `zimmRootVarsCss` block into a shared export so `_app-config` and the decorator share one definition (DRY).

**Owner:** Integration (`.storybook` change) · **Benefits:** Han's component stories · **Priority:** low — cosmetic in Storybook only, zero production impact.

---

That's the whole note. Want me to place it — in the PR description when I open it, as a standalone Jira ticket for Integration, or leave it here for you to route?

content.text:
The evidence answers it cleanly. Here's the net effect.

## The foundation exposes two token surfaces — the limitation touches only one, only in Storybook

| Surface | How a dev uses it | Resolves in app? | Resolves in Storybook? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Chakra tokens** (the sanctioned path) | `textStyle="body1"`, `color="text.default"`, `px="m"`, `<Button variant="primary">` | ✅ | ✅ |
| **`.zimm-*` global classes** | `className="zimm-text-h1"` | ✅ | ❌ |

And `css.md` is unambiguous: **"Chakra UI props first… Chakra token system"**. The `.zimm-*` classes are documented only as an *internal registry* (frozenFiles/protectedFiles), never advertised as a dev-facing API. The **only** `.zimm-*` usage in the whole codebase is one `zimm-grid` in a story. So the path that breaks is the path devs are explicitly steered *away* from.

## Net effect on the manual build, by how devs actually work

**Primary loop — building against `npm start` (the running app): zero effect.** Layer 6 proved every `--zimm-*` resolves in-app. Whatever a dev builds, they see it correctly in their main dev loop.

**Reference material — the 3 Foundation stories: zero effect.** They're Chakra-token based; Layer 4 confirmed 14/14 render correctly. The thing devs open to learn "what's the token for a product name" works.

**New components built the sanctioned way (Chakra tokens), viewed in Storybook: zero effect.** `textStyle`/`color`/`space` all resolve there.

So for a developer following project conventions, the practical DX is **unaffected**. That's the honest headline.

## Where it *does* bite — two narrow cases

1. **Viewing the shared component overrides in Storybook.** `button.ts` mixes Chakra tokens (`bg: 'text.default'` — resolves) with `var(--zimm-*)` (`fontSize`, `lineHeight`, `letterSpacing`, `borderWidth` — don't resolve in SB). So the **Button story renders subtly off** — brand font-size/border fall back to defaults — while being correct in the app. Today that's *one* story (Button); it grows as Han adds component stories.

2. **A dev who goes off-path and uses a `.zimm-*` class**, then checks it in Storybook — sees it render unstyled.

## The real risk isn't breakage — it's a **misleading signal**

The danger is a dev sees a component look wrong *in Storybook*, doesn't know it's a known harness gap, and either:
- burns time debugging a non-bug, or
- worse, "fixes" it by **hardcoding** the value — the exact anti-pattern `css.md` forbids, eroding the design system this branch exists to establish.

That's a low-probability, moderate-cost papercut. It doesn't block anyone; it can waste an hour and quietly damage token discipline if hit blind.

## What this tells you about the note

The risk is **developer confusion**, not an Integration config gap in the abstract. So the note's audience isn't only Integration — **the manual builders need it too**, and it needs to be where a confused dev will actually look. That reframes placement:

- **A one-line caveat in the theme/Storybook context** (a `theme/README` or a comment in `.storybook/preview.tsx`) so a dev who sees an off-looking Storybook render immediately learns why → prevents the hardcode trap. *This is the high-value placement.*
- The fuller note (fix + ownership) → PR description + Integration ticket, as before.

Net verdict: **not a blocker for the manual build, and not critical to fix before merge** — the primary loop and reference stories are clean. Its main cost is avoidable confusion, and the cheapest mitigation is *documentation aimed at devs*, not the `.storybook` code change (which stays Integration's call).

Want me to (a) add that one-line dev-facing caveat now (low-risk, non-Tier-1 if I put it in a `theme/README.md`), and (b) route the full note to the PR + an Integration ticket?

I have the full history now. Here are your three answers.

## 1. The gap/limitation

**Storybook runs fine — the limitation is rendering *fidelity*, not a broken Storybook.** The `--zimm-*` CSS custom properties are injected onto `:root` by **`_app-config` only** (app runtime). `.storybook/preview.tsx` mounts a bare `<ChakraProvider>` with no such injection, so in Storybook:

- ❌ the **component overrides that use `var(--zimm-*)`** — `button.ts` (7 refs), `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` — render with **unresolved** font-size/border (fall back to defaults)
- ❌ the **36 `.zimm-*` global classes** (153 `var()` refs) are inert
- ✅ the **3 Foundation stories** are unaffected — they use Chakra tokens (`textStyle`, `color`), which resolve everywhere

## 2. What's needed to "get it up and running"

Two senses — be clear which:

**(a) To run Storybook** — nothing. It already builds and runs:
```
npm run storybook        # dev server on :6006
npm run build-storybook  # static build
```
I ran the test-runner in Layer 4 — **14/14 stories rendered**, a11y clean. It's operational today.

**(b) To close the var-resolution gap** — one change: add a decorator to **`.storybook/preview.tsx`** injecting the same `:root { --zimm-* }` block `_app-config` uses (extract to a shared `theme/` module for DRY). That's the fix we've been discussing. `.storybook/` is Tier 1 (Integration-owned).

## 3. How current Storybook differs from Jersey's initial commit (`6c608b1`)

I confirmed all 3 commits are **Jersey Perez** (2026-08-12), initial = `6c608b1`. Comparing that to now:

| Aspect | Jersey's initial `6c608b1` | Now `c245ebb` | Changed by |

At the initial commit those overrides used resolvable Chakra tokens, so the **Button story actually rendered correctly then** — the "align to `--zimm-*` surfaces" refactor is what made the Button story render subtly-off in Storybook. Evidence is in. Here's what the discovery changes.

## The core correction: Han is a **consumer**, not the fixer

Han's Button component states it outright — *"all states (hover, pressed, disabled, focused) are handled via the Chakra theme in `theme/components/button.ts`."* And his branch touches **none** of the files the deferred items live in (`button.ts`, `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `foundation/colour.ts`, `zimmTokens.ts`). His F2R components sit **on top of** this branch's foundation + overrides and assume they're correct.

So "Han will handle #1/#4a" is **disproven — exactly like #2 was.** None of the four will be fixed as a side effect of F2R. They all live in surfaces this branch owns.

## Re-verdict on the 4 remaining items

The real axis isn't "Han vs designer" — it's **"does the POC give the answer, or is the POC itself the problem?"**

| # | Was deferred as… | Actually is… | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **#4a** button height 50/41 | "Han's component" | **This branch — trivial.** The correct value **already ships** as `actionSizes` (52/40) in `foundation/sizes.ts`; `button.ts` just hardcodes 50/41 instead of consuming it. Han's Button inherits whatever button.ts says | POC `buttons.css` = 52/40; token exists; override ignores it |
| **#4b** nav spacing 0.02em | "designer" | **This branch — POC gives the answer.** POC nav = `letterspacing-sm` = **0px**. Prototype 0.02em is the deviation | POC `typography.css` |
| **#1** inverse focus ring | "Han's component" | **This branch/foundation — POC gives the answer.** POC `button.md` specifies inverse focus = `grey-white`; the primitives already exist in this branch. Han's Button expects `button.ts` to handle focus | POC `button.md` |
| **#3** contrast (#969696) | "designer" | **Genuinely designer — POC can't help.** The POC *itself* ships `#969696` for primary-hover with **no contrast flag** (it only flags `#939393` for a different token). The design source is non-compliant, so the designer must pick a **new** value | POC `tokens.md:128` |

## What actually changed

1. **Three of the four (#4a, #4b, #1) flipped from "open/Han's" to "prototype-vs-POC discrepancies with a clear POC answer."** Now that the POC is confirmed in-repo as the F2R authority, these aren't open design questions — they're "this branch's overrides deviate from the design source; align them." #4a is the starkest: the right value is *already a shipped token this branch owns*, the override just doesn't use it.

2. **#3 is the only genuine open design decision** — and the discovery makes that sharper, not softer: the POC is itself non-compliant, so nobody can "align to the POC." A human designer has to choose a new AA-passing hover value and push it to Figma.

3. **All four re-home to: this branch's surfaces (fix location) + UI designer (sign-off).** None are Han's. If left "for Han," they'd orphan exactly like #2 nearly did.

## Does this mean fix them here, like #2?

**No — and this is the key difference from #2.** #2 was pure *plumbing* (an injection mechanism, zero design content) with no owner → safe to fix. #4a/#4b/#1/#3 encode **design values**, which Hard Rule #3 routes through the UI designer, and Jersey explicitly flagged them. So they shouldn't be changed unilaterally.

But the discovery **downgrades three of them from "open work" to "one-line designer confirmations"**:
- #4a: *"POC says 52/40 and we already have the token — wire button.ts to it?"*
- #4b: *"POC says 0px — drop the prototype's 0.02em?"*
- #1: *"POC says inverse focus = grey-white — add the inverse variant?"*

Those are yes/no sign-offs with the answer pre-supplied, then a small follow-up commit. **#3 is the only one needing real design work** (a new value).

## Net

The branch as merged is unaffected — it's still a correct foundation, and these are refinements. But the ownership map is now honest: **there is no "Han will do it" path for any of the five.** #2 and #5 are done; #4a/#4b/#1 are cheap designer confirmations against the POC (fixes land in this branch's surfaces); #3 is genuine designer work. I'd package #4a/#4b/#1 as a single 3-question designer note (with the POC citations) and #3 as its own contrast-decision item — not hand any of them to Han.

Want me to draft that consolidated designer note?

content.text:
Straight answer: **No — not for deciding them, even though we can now cite the answer for three of them.** The gap isn't knowledge; it's authority. Those are two different things, and it's worth separating them cleanly:

| # | Do we *know* the answer? | Are we *authorised* to decide it? |
|---|---|---|
| **#4a** height | ✅ POC = 52/40, and it's already a shipped token (`actionSizes`) | ❌ `button.ts` explicitly says *"Unresolved with the UI designer… prototype values stand"* |
| **#4b** nav spacing | ✅ POC = 0px | ❌ flagged *"pending UI designer sign-off"* |
| **#1** inverse focus | ✅ POC `button.md` = grey-white | ❌ Tier 1 foundation token change; no consumer in this branch yet |
| **#3** contrast | ❌ **no** — POC ships the failing `#969696` with no compliant alternative | ❌ new design value |

For #3 we have **neither** basis nor authority. For #4a/#4b/#1 we have the **reference but not the authority** — and here's why the POC being in-repo doesn't close that gap:

1. **Hard Rule #3 is about process, not knowledge.** *"All design token changes go through the UI designer."* It doesn't say "unless you can cite a source." Knowing the value doesn't confer the right to set it.

2. **The POC is not infallible — it says so itself.** `tokens.md` carries *"Confirm with design system owner"* flags, and #3 proves it ships non-compliant values. So "the POC says 52/40" is *evidence for* a designer decision, not a *substitute* for one.

3. **The prototype-vs-POC conflict is unreconciled design intent we can't resolve.** 50/41 (prototype) vs 52/40 (POC) exist *because* someone hasn't decided which is right. Knowing the POC number doesn't tell us *why* Jersey kept the prototype, or whether the designer actually wants the POC value. Jersey's deferral is a real open item, not an oversight.

4. **Changing these then PRing to develop is exactly the risk the deferral avoids.** Developers build UI against these values immediately. If we ship 52/40 and the designer later confirms 50/41, every component built on it is wrong.

## Why this is different from #2 (which I *did* fix here)

#2 was **pure plumbing** — an injection mechanism, zero design content, no documented deferral, no owner, and **empirically verifiable** (I proved `.zimm-*` resolves). We had both knowledge *and* authority. These four carry **design values**, an **explicit author-deferral to the designer**, and can't be verified by a probe — someone has to *decide*. Different category entirely.

Even #1 — the most temping, since it's a WCAG 2.2 AA compliance gap with a clear POC spec — I'd still hold: it's a Tier 1 token addition with **no consumer in this branch** (nothing here renders focus on a dark surface), so fixing it now is speculative foundation change, against minimal-change discipline. It's real, but it's Han's future dark components that will need it — flag it, don't pre-build it.

## Recommendation

**PR the branch as-is now** — the foundation is complete, correct, and fully tested; none of these four block it. Then:

- Convert the deferrals into **one decision-ready designer note** with the POC citations, so #4a/#4b/#1 become fast yes/no confirmations (*"POC says X, prototype says Y, align?"*) rather than open research.
- Treat **#3 as its own item** — it needs the designer to pick a new AA-passing value, since nothing in the POC or repo supplies one.
- Fixes land as a **follow-up** once signed off — pre-merge on this branch if the designer answers quickly, otherwise a fast-follow. Not blind, not on our authority.

So: we have enough to make the designer's decision *cheap and well-referenced* — not enough to make it *for* them.

═══════════════ PR #47 ═══════════════
TITLE: feat(ci): add version-guard to block downgrades on tag-promoted deploys

# Description

Adds **downgrade protection** to the manually-promoted, tag-based deploy tiers
(`test` / `uat` / `staging` / `prod`). Before a deploy, the guard reads the
environment's last recorded deployed tag and **blocks** a push whose tag is *older*
than what's live; after a successful push it **records** the deployed tag.

Why the recording step: on the GitHub **Team** plan, a deploy's auto-created
Deployment records the *trigger* ref (the default branch), not the deployed tag — so
we record the tag ourselves (an explicit GitHub Deployment) and read it back to compare.

`dev` and `sit` are the continuous auto tiers (no human-picked tag — `dev` deploys
`develop`'s latest, `sit` deploys the gate's commit SHA), so a tag-downgrade guard does
not apply and they are intentionally excluded.

# Linked

- Ticket: tag-based promotion rollout under epic **SFCC-1** (Platform Setup &
  Environments); design in Confluence *Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion
  (GitFlow)* (335216656)
- Sprint: SFCC Sprint 2

# Squad ownership

- [x] Platform / integration

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

Full picture pulled. Here's the report on PR #53.

## Overall posture

| Signal | Result |
|---|---|
| **All CI checks** | ✅ **pass** — E2E localhost, Storybook a11y, Vitest, Tier 1 Frozen-Files guard, Branch Target, Cross-Squad, Tier 2 |
| **CodeRabbit review** | ⚠️ **CHANGES_REQUESTED** — 7 inline comments, all **Major**, none a correctness/functional *defect* |
| **CR pre-merge checks** | 4 passed (incl. Title check ✅) · 1 warning: **Docstring coverage 35.71% < 80%** |
| **Merge gate** | `REVIEW_REQUIRED` — held for CODEOWNERS (Tier-1/2, Squad A/B) |

Per AGENTS.md, CodeRabbit is **advisory** — the real gate is the human code-owner review + CI, which is green.

## The 7 findings, categorised

**A. Expected Tier 1 governance flags (2) — reply, don't change:**
1. `.storybook/preview.tsx:14` — *"Do not modify Storybook config."* The verified-session `.storybook` touch. Reply: exception + only viable integration point (Chakra mangles font-family).
2. `colour.ts:99` (+`spacing.ts`) — *"Do not modify Tier 1 foundation files."* Reply: UI-Designer-owned, ported 1:1 from POC, verified session.

**B. Our already-known deferred designer items (3) — CR independently re-surfaced them, which validates the earlier analysis:**
3. `colour.ts:91` — **contrast 2.96:1** hover → this is **#3**, deferred to designer.
4. `button.ts:49/74-79` — *"keep a visible keyboard focus indicator"* (focus clears outline/boxShadow) → aligns with **#1** (focus ring), deferred.
5. `button.ts:98` — hardcoded button sizing → overlaps **#4a** (50/41 vs POC 52/40), deferred.

**C. Genuine code-quality observations (2):**
6. `globalStyles.ts:78` (+4 more ranges) — *"raw visual values → tokens"* (`-0.14px`, `0.15s`, `80px`, `8px`, `36px`, `2px`). **Legit** — I flagged this same thing in the very first analysis. Tier 2, minor, real.
7. `globalStyles.ts:231` — *"breakpoints may diverge from app thresholds."* **Largely unfounded** — the grid media queries are *derived* from `foundation/gridSystem` (`emToPx(breakpoints.md/xl)`), not hardcoded. Reply-and-explain, not a change.

**Plus** the docstring-coverage warning (35.71%) — advisory; the theme files are token data, not logic, so JSDoc density is naturally low. Not a blocker.

## The honest read

- **Zero functional defects.** Nothing CR raised breaks anything — it's 2 governance flags (expected), 3 of our own deferred designer items (CR confirming our judgement), and 2 code-quality nits (1 legit-minor, 1 mostly unfounded).
- **CI is fully green**, including the Tier 1 Frozen-Files guard — the automated governance passed; CR's Tier 1 comments are the *soft* signal, the CODEOWNERS review is the *hard* gate.
- Note: CR reported its own **ESLint tool-run failures** on 3 files — that's CR's sandbox ESLint failing to resolve config; our `npm run lint` (changed files) and the CI Vitest/Storybook jobs are green, so it's a CR-environment artifact, not real.

## What's needed next (AGENTS.md rule)

Every CR finding needs an **in-thread reply** — fixed or explained — or it re-flags forever. My proposed disposition:
- **A (governance ×2):** reply with the exception/ownership justification. No change.
- **B (deferred ×3):** reply pointing to the designer follow-ups (contrast/focus/height) tracked in `projectState.md`. No change on this branch (designer-gated, as we established).
- **C6 (globalStyles hardcoded):** legit — could tokenize now (Tier 2, our file) *or* reply as a follow-up. Your call.

V&V complete — all evidence verified against code + POC. Final loose ends closed: `-0.14px` is faithful (POC `typography.css:183`), the POC focus spec is confirmed (*"Outline only; no background change"* + outline ring, offset 2px/3px), and `marcelannavarro` is confirmed in `tier-1-approvers`.

# V&V of CodeRabbit's 7 findings — verified disposition

| # | CR finding | V&V verdict | Evidence | Our approach |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `.storybook/preview.tsx` — don't modify | **Accurate flag, authorized change** | Only integration point (Chakra mangles font-family, proven); verified session confirmed | **Reply, no change** |
| 2 | `button.ts` — focus indicator inadequate | **✅ CORRECT — real defect** | Primary `_focusVisible`: `#191919→#000000` + `outline:none` = imperceptible (WCAG 2.4.7 fail); **contradicts POC** (`button.md:71,103`: "outline only; no bg change" + ring) | **Reconsider — see below** |
| 3 | `button.ts:98` — hardcoded sizing | **Accurate** | `h:'50px'/'41px'` (POC=52/40), `py:'5px'` (no token) — the #4a deviation | **Defer (designer), POC-cited** |
| 4 | `colour.ts`/`spacing.ts` — Tier 1 | **Accurate flag, authorized** | Foundation, UI-Designer-owned; values ported 1:1 from POC; verified session | **Reply, no change** |
| 5 | `colour.ts:91` — contrast 2.96:1 | **Accurate** | `bgHover #969696` + `#ffffff` = 2.96:1; **POC itself ships this** (non-compliant source) | **Defer — designer picks new value (#3)** |
| 6 | `globalStyles` — raw values → tokens | **Faithful port — rebut** | **All 6 values byte-match POC**: `80px`(buttons.css:23), `0.15s`(:30), `8px`(:193), `36px`(form-fields:24), `2px`(common:68), `-0.14px`(typography:183) | **Reply — tokenizing exceeds the POC (designer's call)** |
| 7 | `globalStyles:231` — breakpoints diverge | **❌ INCORRECT** | Grid is **derived** from `foundation/gridSystem` (`emToPx(breakpoints.md/xl)`) — cannot diverge; code comment says so | **Reply — factually rebut** |
| — | Docstring 35.71% < 80% | Advisory warning | Theme files are token *data*, not logic | **Note, no action (not CI-enforced)** |

## What the V&V changed

The exhaustive pass **held our approach on 6 of 8** but changed two:

**#7 → we can firmly rebut.** CodeRabbit is factually wrong: the grid breakpoints are the *same* foundation source as `theme.breakpoints`, derived via `emToPx()`. Not a judgement call — provably cannot diverge.

**#2 → this is the one that matters.** It is **not** the same as our deferred #1 (inverse focus). CR caught that the **primary (light-mode) button focus is broken for everyone**: `#191919→#000000` with `outline:none` is an invisible focus state = WCAG 2.4.7 failure, on the single most-used component. And crucially, it's a **port error, not a deliberate deferral** — Jersey's comments defer heights/transition, but never focus; the branch silently deviated from the POC, which *explicitly* mandates an outline ring (`border-focus`, offset 2px/3px, no bg change). The POC changelog even says *"fixed focus state."*

## Recommendation on #2 (the only actionable one)

Unlike #3/#4a (genuine "which value does the designer want?" questions), **#2 has no ambiguity**: the POC unambiguously specifies the correct accessible focus, the current state fails WCAG, and the fix uses primitives already in our foundation (`border-focus`, `grey-white`, `border-width`). That makes it a **defect-correction to match the documented design source**, not a new design decision.

So my verified position shifts: **#2 is worth fixing on this branch**, not deferring — it's an accessibility compliance fix (AGENTS.md mandates WCAG 2.2 AA) with a spec-defined answer, in our Tier 2 `button.ts`, using existing tokens. The counter-argument is our "don't touch design surfaces without designer" discipline — but that discipline was for *ambiguous value choices*, and this is an unambiguous a11y fix to the POC spec.

## Net

- **5 findings → reply-and-close** (2 governance authorized, 1 faithful-port defense #6, 1 rebuttal #7, plus docstring note).
- **2 findings → deferred designer items** (#3 contrast value, #4a heights) — POC-cited, genuinely designer's call.
- **1 finding → #2, recommend FIX** — real WCAG defect, POC-specified fix, our own file.

Your call on #2: **fix it now** (I'll implement the POC's outline-ring focus per `button.md:103` and loop-verify), or **defer with the rest** for consistency. Then I'll draft all 7 in-thread replies to post on the PR. Which way on #2?

Good to pin this down clearly. "Deferred to designer" means **design-value decisions that Hard Rule #3 says only the UI designer can make** — we can *cite the answer* from the POC for most, but we can't *decide* them. Here's the full set and what actually happens with them.

## The deferred items

| Item | Where it lives | Current (branch) | Target | Why it's the designer's call | CR-flagged? |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Primary hover contrast** | `colour.ts` / `zimmTokens` | `#969696` on white = **2.96:1** (fails AA) | *unknown* | The POC itself ships this non-compliant value — no correct answer exists to copy; designer must pick a **new** AA-passing colour at source | ✅ `colour.ts:91` |
| **Button heights** | `button.ts` | `50/41px` (prototype) | `52/40px` (POC; token already ships) | Prototype-vs-POC conflict; designer confirms which is canonical | ✅ `button.ts:98` |
| **Nav letter-spacing** | `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` | `0.02em` (prototype) | `0px` (POC) | Same prototype-vs-POC conflict | ❌ (not flagged by CR) |
| **Inverse focus ring** | `button.ts` / `zimmTokens` | light-mode only | grey-white on dark (POC) | Needs an inverse variant + ties into Han's inverse component | ❌ (light focus was flagged — now fixed) |
| **`text.inverseGrey`** | `colour.ts:52` | `#969696` | `#969696` vs `#939393` — POC self-contradicts | POC is ambiguous; only the designer can resolve | ❌ |
| **Motion tokens** | `motion.ts` | provisional values | POC says *"PLACEHOLDER, pending sign-off"* | POC explicitly marks them unfinished | ❌ |

Two of these are the CodeRabbit findings in the reply plan (contrast, heights); the other four we surfaced ourselves during the V&V.

## What we're doing with them — the honest lifecycle

**1. Not fixed on this branch — deliberately.** They're design-token *value* decisions. Changing them without designer sign-off is exactly what Hard Rule #3 forbids, and (for the prototype-vs-POC ones) we don't know which value the designer actually wants.

**2. They do NOT block PR #53.** The branch ships the foundation as a *faithful port* of the POC — the deviations are the prototype's, honestly flagged in-code. The foundation is usable for the manual UI build as-is; these are refinements.

**3. Where they're currently tracked** — two places, both committed:
- `.docs/memory/projectState.md:46` — the "Open with the UI designer: …" line (names contrast, inverse focus, button-height/nav deviations).
- In-code comments at each site (`button.ts`, `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `colour.ts:52`, `motion.ts`).

**4. What resolving one looks like:** UI designer decides the value → a small follow-up commit to *this branch's own surfaces* (`foundation/*` or `theme/components/*`, with sign-off) → done. None of it is Han's (his components *consume* these; he doesn't set them).

## The honest gap

You declined a standalone designer note earlier, and there's **no Jira ticket** (this work is ad hoc). So right now these items **only live in `projectState.md` + code comments** — which means they'll *sit there* until someone actively raises them with the designer. Nothing automatically drives them forward.

So the real question for you: **how do you want to drive them?**
- **(a) Leave as-is** — captured in `projectState.md`; you/the team raise them with the designer ad hoc when convenient.
- **(b) I raise them now** — draft a short consolidated message to the UI designer (the 6 items, current vs POC value, the one that needs a genuinely new value) — *not* a repo doc, just a message you can send.
- **(c) File lightweight tickets** — one per item under the design-system work, if you want them tracked formally despite the ad hoc nature.

My recommendation: **(b)** — the contrast one (#3) is a live WCAG AA failure that ships in the token values, so it genuinely wants a designer decision sooner rather than sitting in `projectState.md`. The rest can ride along in the same message. Want me to draft it?

content.text:
Both are grounded in the repo now. They're two *different* design references the branch drew from, with different authority:

## The POC (a.k.a. "the Handover")

**What:** the `Zimmermann-Handover` repo — specifically `02-design/library` — which is the **F2R (Figma-to-React) workflow proof-of-concept**. It's the design system **machine-extracted from Figma** (`<!-- managed-by: /extract -->`, source: `Zimmermann_Design_System_2026`). It contains the authoritative token CSS (`colors/typography/spacing/buttons/form-fields.css`), component specs (`button.md` etc.), the contract, and a viewer.

**Authority:** this is the **source of truth** the branch claims to port "1:1." When I said "verified 122/122 against the POC," this is what I compared against. In-code, it's called "the Handover" (e.g., `button.ts:85`: *"The Handover's action tokens specify 52px…"*).

## The prototype

**What:** `zimm-prototype.vercel.app` — per `architecture.md:146`: *"Desktop prototype … is AI-generated and desktop-only — also not a signed-off final design."* A separate visual mockup, **not** the Figma design system.

**Authority:** explicitly **not authoritative** — AI-generated, desktop-only, unsigned. But the branch author (Jersey) pulled several values from it — button heights `50/41`, nav letter-spacing `0.02em`, header layout details, the font fallback stack — visible all through the code comments (`button.ts`, `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts`, `fonts.ts`, `motion.ts`).

## Why this matters for the deferred items

Every "deferred to designer" item is exactly a spot where **the prototype and the POC disagree, and the branch chose the prototype's value**:

| | POC (authoritative) | Prototype (branch chose this) |
|---|---|---|
| Button height | 52 / 40px | **50 / 41px** |
| Nav letter-spacing | 0px | **0.02em** |

The branch's own comments say it kept the prototype value "pending UI designer sign-off." So "reconcile with the designer" = *the designer decides whether the authoritative POC or the not-signed-off prototype wins* for each. In most cases the POC (Figma extraction) should win — but that's the designer's call, not ours, because the prototype was presumably shown/approved visually and we don't know why the divergence exists.

## One honest caveat on the POC's own provenance

The extract source URL in `tokens.md` reads `figma.com/design/…/MCP-Test--Don-t-Use`. That "Don't Use" label is a flag that even the POC's Figma origin may be a **test file**, not the final signed-off design — which is *another* reason these value decisions genuinely need the UI designer to confirm against the real, current Figma, rather than us treating either the POC or the prototype as final.

So in short: **POC = the Figma-extracted F2R handover (authoritative-ish, what we ported); prototype = an AI-generated Vercel mockup (not signed off, source of the deviations).** The deferred items are where those two disagree and only the designer can rule.

content.text:
Decisive evidence — and the answer is **no, they won't be overwritten by Han's F2R**, with an important implication.

## Why not

Three verified facts:

1. **Han's branch touches none of the 3 files** the deferred items live in — `button.ts`, `header.ts`, `listMenu.ts` all confirmed untouched.

2. **His Button *consumes* `button.ts`, doesn't override it.** His JSDoc is explicit: *"all states (hover, pressed, disabled, focused) are handled via the Chakra theme in `overrides/app/theme/components/button.ts`."* His component just passes `variant`/`size` through to Chakra, which reads the heights from `button.ts`.

3. **F2R has no theme-code generator.** Every F2R skill is design-side — `extract`, `handover`, `deploy-viewer`, `deploy-catalog`, `stitch-pages`, `start-prototype`, `workshop`. There is **no** skill or automation that writes the PWA's Chakra `theme/components/*.ts`. F2R produces specs, tokens, viewers, and prototypes — not theme override code (Jersey hand-wrote `button.ts`).

So nothing in Han's stream regenerates or replaces these files.

## The implication that actually matters (it's the opposite of "overwritten")

Because Han **consumes** `button.ts`, the deferred deviation **propagates into his F2R components** — his Button renders at **50/41 too**, not the POC's 52/40, because it inherits this branch's override. Same for anything that consumes the nav overrides.

So these aren't:
- ❌ "throwaway if we fix now" (Han would redo them) — he won't touch them, and
- ❌ "will be superseded by F2R" — F2R has no mechanism to.

They're:
- ✅ **shared foundation values that persist until a human deliberately edits `button.ts`/`header.ts`/`listMenu.ts`** — and until then, the prototype deviations flow *downstream* into both this branch's rendering **and** Han's F2R components.

## What that means for the decision

This actually **strengthens the case to resolve them with the designer** rather than leave them indefinitely — "defer" here does *not* mean "F2R will handle it," it means "nobody handles it until someone drives the designer decision." Left alone, `50/41` and `0.02em` become the de facto values across the whole UI build, prototype-sourced, forever.

The disposition is unchanged (still designer-gated — we can't unilaterally decide prototype vs POC), but the framing flips: this is the shared root both streams render from, so reconciling it to the POC with the designer is worth doing sooner, not something that self-resolves.

**Caveat on my certainty:** this holds for Han's *current* branch + the *existing* F2R skill set. If the F2R workflow later adds a "generate PWA theme from POC" step, that calculus changes — but no such mechanism exists today.

Given this, do you want me to raise the deferred items with the designer now (the short consolidated message), since they won't resolve themselves and they propagate into Han's work?
